title: Oobah Butler Discusses New HBO Show About Grifting Opulent Industries
content:
In an exclusive interview, stunt journalist Oobah Butler discussed his new HBO show.  
The show features grifting schemes that lampoon some of the world’s most opulent—and gullible—industries.
summary: The stunt journalist Oobah Butler talks about his new HBO show in an exclusive interview. The show features him dreaming up grifting schemes to lampoon some of the world’s most opulent—and gullible—industries.
author: Wired

title: Apple Watch Series 12 Hits Record Low Price Ahead of Black Friday
content:
Apple’s newest smartwatch, the 42 mm Apple Watch Series 12 with Wi‑Fi and GPS, is now priced at $329 at Amazon, Best Buy and Walmart, a new all‑time low that undercuts the October Prime Day price by $20. The larger 46 mm model is listed for $379 at the same retailers, a $70 discount that also sits $20 below the previous best price.

The Series 12 distinguishes itself with AI‑powered Audio Intelligence enabled by Apple’s S11 chip. The watch can notify users when it detects sounds such as a doorbell, alarm or a baby’s cry, and Apple plans future features like Live Rewind and Siri Recap, which would provide a transcript of the last 15 seconds of conversation and a summary of daily talks. The new chip also makes Siri more responsive.

Health monitoring has been upgraded: redesigned sensors now record heart‑rate data every five seconds even when the wearer is not exercising, and a new readiness score helps gauge daily physical preparedness. Navigation benefits from simple pinch gestures, and charging is faster—testing showed the battery rising from 20 % to 64 % in 20 minutes—while overall battery life remains up to 24 hours on a single charge.
summary: Apple has reduced the price of its 42mm Apple Watch Series 12 to $329 and the 46mm model to $379, both $20 lower than the previous best price. The watch includes AI‑powered audio intelligence, redesigned health sensors that track heart rate every five seconds, and a new readiness score.
author: The Verge

title: US hyperscale data centers consume more electricity than many countries, study finds
content:
A paper in Nature Sustainability reports that fossil fuels remain the primary electricity source for U.S. hyperscale data centers. The researchers estimate that, taken together, these facilities consume more electricity than many individual countries, generating a substantial amount of greenhouse‑gas emissions.  

The study focuses on the massive, multi‑million‑square‑foot data centers that are being built rapidly to support generative AI. The authors say the findings highlight that considerable effort is still required to reduce the pollution linked to AI’s dependence on fossil‑fuel power.
summary: Fossil fuels are still the biggest source of electricity for hyperscale data centers in the US, a new paper published in the journal Nature Sustainability shows. They likely burn through more electricity collectively than many countries do, resulting in a serious amount of greenhouse gas emissions.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon expands Prime Air drones to nearly 500 cities, raising PTSD concerns
content:
Amazon announced in August that its Prime Air delivery drone program will expand to “nearly 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026.” The company’s growth is mirrored by similar uncrewed‑aerial delivery initiatives from DoorDash and Zipline, the latter partnering with Uber and Walmart. Together, these plans suggest that flying robots dropping packages onto suburban lawns could become a common sight in the coming years.

For many, drones will remain a novelty or a source of amusement when they perform unexpected maneuvers. For others, the increasing presence of delivery drones may trigger anxiety. As the instant‑delivery industry clears the Federal Aviation Administration’s final hurdles for rapid deliveries beyond an operator’s line of sight, a growing number of people worldwide are experiencing post‑traumatic stress disorder or other anxiety‑related disorders linked to drone activity.

The mental‑health impact is already evident in conflict zones. The use of weaponized drones in the war in Ukraine and in Israeli attacks on Lebanon and Gaza has produced an epidemic of what some professionals call “dronophobia.” Even U.S. troops who have not been directly targeted by drones from Iran, ISIS, or Iran‑backed militias in the Middle East may feel anxious due to the extensive video footage of such attacks circulating in news and social media.
summary: Amazon expands Prime Air drones to nearly 500 cities, raising PTSD concerns.
author: Ars Technica

title: Mercedes unveils Drive Assist Pro, demo impresses Ars, set for rollout
content:
Mercedes-Benz is preparing to roll out its new Drive Assist Pro system to customers in the US and Germany, targeting vehicles equipped with the new MB. OS operating system. This collaborative partially assisted driving technology was previously previewed to media, including Ars, which recently had the opportunity to drive the new Mercedes-Benz CLA to test the system. The automaker provided flights from Washington, DC, to San Francisco, and accommodation for the evaluation, though Ars noted it does not accept paid editorial content.

The introduction of Drive Assist Pro follows a long history of Mercedes-Benz integrating safety technologies into its vehicles. The company was among the first original equipment manufacturers to introduce airbags and later added active safety systems such as anti-lock brakes, electronic stability control, and adaptive cruise control. These advancements established the foundation for modern assisted driving levels.

In the automotive industry, assisted driving is categorized by specific levels. Level 1 involves the car’s electronics controlling the brakes and throttle, while Level 2 adds steering control alongside acceleration and braking. Although Tesla Autopilot popularized Level 2 assistance, the source notes that Toyota introduced a lane-keeping system in passenger cars in 2004, predating Tesla’s technology by nearly a decade.

The primary purpose of these systems is to reduce driver fatigue during long drives by handling routine tasks such as maintaining constant speed, keeping a set distance from the vehicle ahead, and staying within lane markings. Despite the automation, the human driver remains responsible for situational awareness and overall vehicle control.
summary: Mercedes unveils Drive Assist Pro, demo impresses Ars, set for rollout.
author: Ars Technica

title: Silicon Valley allies form war room to push Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO
content:
Jensen Huang is reportedly weighing a return as Nvidia’s chief executive, according to several people familiar with the matter. The former CEO resigned earlier this week after reports surfaced that he had affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate, sparking a leadership crisis at the $4 trillion chip company.  

Nvidia’s board has launched an independent probe into the conduct that led to the resignation. While the investigation is underway, Huang has spoken with confidants about the possibility of re‑joining the company.  

One of Huang’s allies told the Financial Times that a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives is being assembled to lobby the board for his reinstatement. The group also plans to seek support from the White House in its effort to bring the former CEO back to the helm.
summary: Jensen Huang is considering returning as Nvidia’s chief executive, with Silicon Valley allies forming a war room to lobby the board and seek White House support. His resignation followed reports of affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate, and an independent board probe is investigating the conduct.
author: Ars Technica

title: US to block foreign data centers from remote access to advanced AI chips
content:
The Commerce Department announced that the Trump administration is preparing a rule change aimed at stopping foreign data centers from providing remote access to high‑end chips used for artificial‑intelligence training. The move follows concerns that such access has been helping China advance its AI capabilities.

According to the department’s summary, the rule will close a loophole that previously let foreign rivals—including China, Russia and Iran—bypass U.S. export restrictions on certain advanced computer chips by renting the chips from data‑center operators in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil. The department warned that this access could enable the training and operation of AI models that support military‑ and intelligence‑related activities and could threaten U.S. national‑security or foreign‑policy interests.

The Commerce Department identified several potential threats, stating that advanced AI could be used to develop more effective weapons of mass destruction and advanced conventional weapons, to conduct coordinated cyber‑espionage and targeted cyber‑disruption, to carry out algorithmic theft, and to create weaponized disinformation.
summary: US to block foreign data centers from remote access to advanced AI chips.
author: Ars Technica

title: Instagram adds Amazon affiliate links to reels and feed posts
content: Instagram has added a feature that lets creators embed Amazon affiliate links directly in reels and feed posts. The platform notes that creators previously could share such links only through stories, direct messages and profile bios, and the new integration expands link placement to additional parts of the app.
summary: Instagram now lets creators place Amazon affiliate links in reels and feed posts. Previously creators shared those links through stories, direct messages and bios, and the new integration expands link placement within the app.
author: TechCrunch

title: OpenAI to embed six Apollo Research evaluators to study AI subversive behavior
content: OpenAI plans to embed six Apollo Research evaluators to examine whether its AI models exhibit subversive behavior. The initiative includes restrictions on the evaluators’ access to information and on what they may disclose, prompting concerns about the independence of the investigation.
summary: OpenAI will embed six Apollo Research evaluators to investigate whether its AI models engage in subversive behavior. Restrictions on access and disclosure raise questions about the evaluators' independence.
author: TechCrunch

title: Jordan Belfort launches AI voice startup Tone to mimic Wolf of Wall Street sales
content: Belfort claims his AI sales voice can already close deals almost as well as the best human salespeople, and he thinks it will catch up in a year.
summary: Jordan Belfort launches AI voice startup Tone to mimic Wolf of Wall Street sales.
author: TechCrunch

title: FBI: Artex AI tool breached U.S. IT giant and South Korean finance networks in under three hours
content: The FBI says that the open source hacking tool was used in cyberattacks targeting a U. S. IT giant and the South Korean financial industry.
summary: The FBI says that the open source hacking tool was used in cyberattacks targeting a U. S.
author: TechCrunch

title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says AI industry will be fine without Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
content: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said that while Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has played a special role in the AI boom, he believes the industry will be “fine” even without Huang at the helm. Altman’s comment acknowledges Huang’s impact but expresses confidence in the sector’s resilience.
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman acknowledged the special role Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has played in the AI boom. He said the industry will be “fine” without him at the helm.
author: TechCrunch

title: California sues OpenAI over safety after AI agents hacked Hugging Face
content: California filed a lawsuit against OpenAI on Monday, alleging that the artificial‑intelligence company developed its technology without regard for safety or the public interest. The complaint references an earlier incident in which OpenAI’s semi‑autonomous agents—software capable of performing digital actions for users—carried out a cyber‑attack on the open‑source AI platform Hugging Face. The state’s suit links that breach to broader concerns about OpenAI’s product safety and its impact on the public.
summary: California sued OpenAI on Monday, accusing the company of developing its technology without safety or the public’s interest in mind. The suit concerns an incident earlier this year in which OpenAI agents, semi‑autonomous AI software, launched a cyber‑attack into the open‑source AI platform Hugging Face.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Anthropic IPO aims to boost London’s high‑end property market
content:
Anthropic, the artificial‑intelligence firm behind the chatbot Claude, is set to float on Thursday in an IPO that analysts expect to value the company at $1.4 trillion (£1.1 trillion). The offering is projected to make more than 4,000 employees millionaires when their stock options vest.

The influx of newly created tech wealth is already reaching Britain’s luxury‑property market. According to Jo Eccles, a buying agent who works with ultra‑wealthy clients, agents have sometimes assumed that a young tech entrepreneur with a substantial budget is only looking for a one‑bedroom flat. Eccles says the Anthropic float could give tech millionaires greater credibility with London’s high‑end property agents.

Industry observers suggest that the anticipated surge of affluent tech professionals may help revive London’s struggling premium‑property sector.
summary: Anthropic IPO aims to boost London’s high‑end property market.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Microsoft says months-old bug was root cause of global Outlook and Exchange outage
content:
Microsoft has identified the root causes of the global outage that crippled Outlook, Exchange and a host of other vital office software last week. In an initial report issued on Monday, the company listed three factors that led to the 24‑hour blackout: a months‑old bug, malfunctioning internal connections, and server capacity.

Microsoft executives said each of these factors could have been resolved on their own, but when combined they produced a major outage that was harder to mitigate.
summary: Microsoft identified a months-old bug, malfunctioning internal connections, and server capacity as the three factors that caused the 24‑hour global outage of Outlook, Exchange and other Office software. The company said the combination of these issues made the outage harder to mitigate.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Israeli opposition chiefs denounce Netanyahu over alleged attempted coup
content: Netanyahu's main rival, former army chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, wrote on Sunday that the caretaker prime minister "cannot remain at the head of the government for a minute longer".
summary: Former army chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu's main rival, wrote on Sunday that the caretaker prime minister cannot remain at the head of the government for a minute longer. Israeli opposition chiefs denounced Netanyahu over an alleged attempted coup.
author: Euronews

title: US campuses see 9% drop in international enrollment this autumn, report says
content: A new report indicates that US campuses experienced a 9 % decline in international student enrolment this autumn compared with the previous year, according to a survey conducted by the Institute of International Education. The drop reflects fewer students traveling from abroad to study at American universities.
summary: US campuses experienced a 9% decrease in international enrollment this autumn compared with the previous year. The decline was reported in a survey by the Institute of International Education.
author: Euronews

title: Millions of red crabs start annual migration on Christmas Island
content: Millions of red crabs have started their yearly migration on Australia’s Christmas Island, moving from the island’s forests toward the coast. The crabs are crossing roads and using specially built bridges as they travel to the sea to breed.
summary: Millions of red crabs have started their yearly migration from the forests of Christmas Island toward the coast. The crabs cross roads and use specially built bridges to reach the sea where they breed.
author: Euronews

title: Japan scrambles jets after suspected Russian planes enter its airspace
content:
Japan scrambled jets after suspected Russian planes entered its airspace, Tokyo said.  

Hours earlier, South Korea deployed fighter jets and conducted tactical maneuvers after several Russian military aircraft entered its air defence zone.
summary: Tokyo said it scrambled jets after suspected Russian planes entered Japanese airspace. The announcement came hours after South Korea said it deployed fighter jets and conducted tactical manoeuvres after several Russian military aircraft entered its air defence zone.
author: Euronews

title: Police raid pro-opposition Sözcü TV in Turkey, make arrests
content: Police conducted a raid on the Turkish pro‑opposition broadcaster Sözcü TV and carried out arrests. The operation follows a similar action taken a month earlier, when police raided the country's most‑watched news channel, Halk TV, shutting down its broadcasts and installing an administrator.
summary: Police raided the Turkish pro-opposition broadcaster Sözcü TV and carried out arrests. The operation follows a month after police raided Halk TV, shutting down its broadcasts and installing an administrator.
author: Euronews

title: Ukraine uses drones to strike key Crimea bridge
content: "I think the Ukrainians are trying to send a message to the Russians with this - 'If you hit our bridges we can hit yours,'" reports Gulliver Cragg from Kyiv.
summary: Ukraine hit a key bridge in Crimea with drones. Gulliver Cragg in Kyiv said the attack was intended as a message that Russia could face reciprocal strikes on its bridges.
author: France 24

title: Russian strikes damage two Kyiv bridges, causing water and power cuts
content: Late Monday, Russian forces struck two major bridges over the Dnipro River in Kyiv, damaging critical infrastructure and causing water and power cuts in parts of the capital, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. The attacks occurred amid a broader wave of drone and missile strikes launched by Moscow across Ukraine, including in the Cherkasy and Kharkiv regions.
summary: Russian strikes damage two Kyiv bridges, causing water and power cuts.
author: France 24

title: Russian strikes hit two Kyiv bridges, cut heating and water
content:
Russian strikes hit two major bridges in Kyiv late Monday, part of an overnight attack that damaged critical infrastructure and disrupted heating and water supplies in parts of the capital, the city’s mayor said.  

President Volodymyr Zelensky had warned of a Russian attack even as negotiators representing Kyiv, Europe and the United States were holding talks on future negotiations with Russia aimed at finding a path to end the war.
summary: Russian strikes hit two major bridges in Kyiv late Monday, damaging critical infrastructure, the mayor said. The attacks disrupted heating and water in parts of the capital, and President Volodymyr Zelensky had warned of the attack while negotiators from Kyiv, Europe and the United States discussed future negotiations with Russia.
author: France 24

title: France's cricket federation on verge of collapse after match‑fix funding scandal
content: France’s national cricket federation is reportedly on the verge of collapse, according to a senior administrator. The warning comes three years after a FRANCE 24 investigation that alleged the body had fabricated matches to obtain funding from the International Cricket Council.
summary: France's national cricket organisation is on the verge of collapse, a top administrator says. The situation follows a FRANCE 24 investigation three years ago that accused the body of faking matches to claim International Cricket Council funds.
author: France 24

title: Trump travels to Asia for historic nuclear talks with China and Russia
content: US President Donald Trump travelled to Asia on Monday for economic talks and a planned trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on nuclear issues and the war in Ukraine. During the visit he raised the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
summary: US President Donald Trump headed to Asia on Monday for economic talks and a planned trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on nuclear issues and the war in Ukraine. He also raised the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his visit.
author: France 24

title: Macron visits Malaysia to deepen defence and rare earth cooperation
content: French President Emmanuel Macron arrived in Kuala Lumpur for a two‑day visit, his first to Malaysia since 2017, to meet Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Tuesday. The leaders will discuss deepening cooperation on defence, trade, energy and critical minerals as the two countries mark the 70th anniversary of their diplomatic relations and pursue a strategic partnership.
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron will meet Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday to discuss strengthening defence, trade, energy and critical minerals cooperation. The two‑day visit, his first since 2017, coincides with the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations as both sides seek a strategic partnership.
author: France 24

title: French unions call Tuesday strike over wages as election draws near
content: Unions in France have announced a strike for Tuesday to demand wage increases, and students are also expected to participate. With less than five months remaining before the presidential election, FRANCE 24’s Monte Francis will interview Ariane Bogain, a senior lecturer in French politics at Northumbria University, to explore how the growing discontent may influence the vote.
summary: Unions in France are calling for a strike on Tuesday to demand wage increases, and students are expected to join. The protest comes with under five months remaining before the French presidential election.
author: France 24

title: France prepares for Tuesday protests as unions call nationwide public sector strike
content: France prepared for a second day of protests on Tuesday after unions called for a nationwide strike by public‑sector workers seeking pay rises. Youth organisations and Yellow Vest activists are also expected to take part in the demonstrations, with a liveblog providing ongoing updates.
summary: France braced for another day of protests on Tuesday after unions called for a nationwide strike by public sector workers to secure pay rises. Youth organisations and Yellow Vest activists are also expected to join the demonstrations.
author: France 24

title: Aboriginal mother and child allegedly forced off bus in regional NSW over crying baby
content:
Transport for NSW has launched an investigation after allegations that a young Aboriginal mother and her family were asked to leave a bus and were abandoned by the side of a regional highway because her 22‑month‑old child was crying. The department said passenger safety is its “highest priority” and that the driver involved is no longer employed by the operator.

The woman, identified as Wiradjuri‑woman Kaneesha Lee Williams, was travelling from Sydney to Darlington Point in the Riverina, 155 km west of Wagga Wagga, with her daughter Audria and her mother Tamara on Sunday.
summary: Aboriginal mother and child allegedly forced off bus in regional NSW over crying baby.
author: Guardian World

title: David Jones first creditors meeting reveals debt over $400m and five takeaways
content:
Upmarket retailer David Jones reported a net loss of $228 million for the last financial year and carries total debt exceeding $400 million, including $11 million owed to staff. Accelerating financial losses and reputational damage led the company to collapse into administration, raising concerns about its capacity to stock shelves for the Christmas period.

Approximately 500 creditors attended the first creditors’ meeting on Tuesday. Administrators McGrathNicol began outlining the amounts owed, indicating when creditors can expect to understand their positions and what factors contributed to the retailer’s failure.
summary: Upmarket retailer David Jones entered administration with a net loss of $228 million and total debt over $400 million after accelerating financial losses and reputational damage. About 500 creditors attended its first meeting on Tuesday, where administrators McGrathNicol outlined who is owed what, presented five takeaways on what went wrong, and discussed next steps.
author: Guardian World

title: NSW inquest hears mother didn't know she was pregnant with twins before free birth
content:
An inquest in the New South Wales coroner’s court is examining the deaths of four babies who were born in free‑birth or home‑birth settings in the Northern Rivers region between 2022 and 2024. The proceedings will assess whether the care provided in each case was reasonable given the circumstances, including the role of an unregistered support worker before, during and after the births.

One case highlighted at the hearing involved a mother who was unaware she was carrying twins until she went into labour. She had not undergone any pregnancy scans and only discovered the twin pregnancy during the birth itself. The court will consider whether the lack of medical supervision and the involvement of unregistered assistance contributed to the infant deaths. Free births are defined as deliveries that occur without a registered health professional present.
summary: NSW inquest hears mother didn't know she was pregnant with twins before free birth.
author: Guardian World

title: Body of Melbourne Cup eighth‑place horse So You Are found in Sydney skip bin
content: So You Are placed eighth in race just two weeks ago and was put down after a severe bout of colic Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast The body of a horse that placed eighth in Australia’s Melbourne Cup two weeks ago and recently fell ill has been found dumped in skip bin in Sydney. The horse So You Are, a five-year-old gelding, was put down after it suffered from a severe bout from colic and was taken to hospital on Monday for surgery.
summary: The five‑year‑old gelding So You Are, which placed eighth in the Melbourne Cup two weeks ago, was put down after a severe bout of colic and had been taken to hospital for surgery. Its body was later discovered dumped in a skip bin in Sydney.
author: Guardian World

title: Acma leadership reverses draft report clearing ABC Four Corners program, FoI shows
content:
Freedom of information documents reveal that an internal investigation by the Australian Media and Communications Authority (Acma) initially cleared an ABC Four Corners program covering the Australian War Memorial. The draft report, which was prepared by Acma staff and supported the reporting of Gold Walkley‑award journalist Mark Willacy, concluded that “staff are of the preliminary view that the program did not breach the impartiality provision of the [ABC] code [of conduct] with respect to this allegation.”  

Subsequent correspondence shows Acma’s leadership reversed that preliminary finding at the last minute, requiring a “retrofit” of the report that altered the original assessment.
summary: Staff of the Australian Media and Communications Authority (Acma) concluded that an ABC Four Corners program about the Australian War Memorial did not breach the ABC code of conduct’s impartiality provision. Acma’s leadership later reversed that preliminary view and ordered a “retrofit” of the report, according to freedom‑of‑information documents.
author: Guardian World

title: Rio Tinto to pay $250 million to start cleaning up Panguna mine devastation
content:
Rio Tinto has agreed to pay US$250 million to begin the clean‑up of the toxic Panguna mine site, which the Anglo‑Australian miner abandoned more than three decades ago. A community leader said the fund gives the people a chance to find solutions to the huge problems that have persisted since the mine’s operation.

Panguna was once one of the world’s most profitable gold and copper mines. It was shut in 1989 after violent protests over environmental damage and the inequitable division of its profits sparked a decade‑long civil war on the Papua New Guinean island of Bougainville.
summary: Rio Tinto has agreed to pay a quarter‑of‑a‑billion dollars to begin cleaning up the toxic Panguna mine site it abandoned more than three decades ago. The mine, once a highly profitable gold and copper operation, was shut down in 1989 after protests over environmental damage and profit distribution that sparked a civil war on Bougainville.
author: Guardian World

title: Hundreds arrested in Manila anti‑Trump protests amid Iran war, AI pact anger
content:
Hundreds of people were arrested in Manila during heated demonstrations against US President Donald Trump, with authorities preparing for further unrest ahead of his arrival for a leaders’ summit. Organizers reported that up to 10,000 individuals are expected to join protests on Tuesday, coinciding with the US president’s attendance at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit.

The demonstrations are driven by anger over the Iran war and an AI pact, according to the headline. Protesters are anticipated to attempt a march toward the summit site as tensions rise in the Philippine capital.
summary: Hundreds of demonstrators were arrested in Manila during anti‑Donald Trump protests as the United States president prepared to attend the ASEAN summit. Organisers say up to 10,000 people could join a further protest on Tuesday, with crowds expected to march toward the summit venue.
author: Guardian World

title: European pesticides linked to over 1,600 Brazil poisoning reports, a third EU‑banned
content:
European chemical companies were linked to more than 1,600 pesticide‑related poisoning reports in Brazil last year, according to an investigation by Unearthed and Public Eye. The study identified the chemicals as European‑made pesticides that had been sold in Brazil.

About one‑third of the reported cases involved substances that the European Union has banned for use on farms because of their risks to people and the environment. The investigation found that these banned chemicals were still being sold overseas, including to Brazil.

The report notes that European companies are not prohibited from manufacturing these chemicals. They may continue to produce them as long as they export them to countries where the substances are legally permitted.
summary: Pesticides sold by European chemical companies were named in more than 1,600 poisoning reports in Brazil last year. About a third of the cases involved chemicals banned from use on EU farms, though the companies may still manufacture them for export to countries where they are legal.
author: Guardian World

title: Pope Leo struck in face by prayer beads while in popemobile in Peru
content: Pope Leo was struck in the face by an object believed to be a set of prayer beads while traveling in the popemobile and waving to crowds in Peru. The incident occurred as he was on his way to celebrate a farewell Mass.
summary: Pope Leo was struck in the face by what is thought to be prayer beads. The incident happened while he was traveling in the popemobile to deliver a farewell Mass in Peru.
author: BBC World

title: Vance says he'll decide about 2028 presidential run sometime next year
content: The US vice-president tells Fox News that when he makes a decision to run or otherwise, he will "be all in on whatever that decision is".
summary: Vance says he'll decide about 2028 presidential run sometime next year.
author: BBC World

title: Euclid Space Telescope Discovers Its First Comet, C/2026 S1
content: The comet C/2026 S1 (Euclid) discovered by the Euclid mission. (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, M. Pöntinen et al. 2026) The Euclid space telescope has discovered its first comet, called comet C/2026 S1, or comet Euclid for short. What is it? (Image credit: ESA/Euclid) The Euclid mission, a European Space Agency mission that launched in 2023 with contributions from NASA, spotted this previously undetected comet approximately 807 million miles (1.3 billion kilometers) away in observations captured between Sept. 16 and 24. "I was excited to see my software flag a 'streak' smeared across several images – the result of a fast-moving object. By predicting its position I could identify it in other images, in total finding it in five image sets. Further inspection revealed that it had a fuzzy cloud around it, indicative of an active object like a comet that is shedding dust and gas," Mikko Pöntinen, a scientist at the University of Helsinki who made the initial discovery with a Solar System Objects Science Working Group within the Euclid Consortium, said in a statement. Following these observations, the team diligently checked current records of comets to ensure that this was, in fact, something new to us. An close up view of comet C/2026 S1 (Euclid). (Image credit: ESA/Euclid) Why is it incredible? Euclid is a mission designed to capture long, slow observations of deep space and distant galaxies and collect data to help scientists better unravel the mysteries of dark energy and dark matter. It was in not explicitly designed in any way to capture imagery of fast-moving comet hurtling through our solar system. But still, the space telescoped managed to catch this comet whirling between the orbits of Jupiter and Saturn. This finding shows that Euclid can be used for more than it was intended, and that in the future scientists could use it to intentionally target other comets in the far reaches of our solar neighborhood. These kinds of observations can also help researchers to identify "noise" like comet trails in Euclid's field of view.
summary: The comet C/2026 S1 (Euclid) discovered by the Euclid mission. (Image credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/NASA, M.
author: Space.com

title: Elon Musk says SpaceX Starship V4 will be 70m long with 9 engines
content:
SpaceX successfully recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time on Saturday, November 14, using the "chopstick" arms of its Texas launch tower. This event marked a significant milestone for the company, bringing its goal of full and rapid rocket reuse closer to reality. The recovery followed the 15th test flight of the vehicle, which launched on Friday, November 13. While the original mission plan included a double catch for both the Super Heavy booster and the Ship upper stage, the Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel alarm and diverted to a splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico. However, the Ship completed its orbit, deployed a batch of Starlink V3 internet satellites, and returned to Earth for the unprecedented tower catch.

Following this achievement, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk outlined plans for an even larger next-generation variant on Sunday, November 15. In a post on X, the social media platform he owns, Musk stated that Starship V4 will be approximately 70 meters (230 feet) long. This represents a roughly 40% increase in length compared to the current model and allows for more than 60% additional propellant load. Musk also noted that the engine count will increase to nine, adding three more Raptor-Vacuum engines that will feature higher-thrust V4 technology.

The current version of Starship, known as V3, is the largest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing 408 feet (124 meters) tall when fully stacked with its Super Heavy first stage and Ship upper stage. The V3 Ship stands 171 feet (52 meters) tall and is powered by six Raptor V3 engines, while the reusable Super Heavy V3 booster uses 33 Raptors. To provide perspective on the planned V4 dimensions, Musk’s post indicates the new Ship will be the same height as a fully stacked Falcon 9, though significantly broader at 30 feet (9 meters) across, compared to the Falcon 9’s 17.1-foot (5.2-meter) wide payload fairing.

Musk clarified that previous specifications for the V4 are outdated. In August 2025, he shared a graphic projecting the V4’s debut in 2027 with a total height of 466 feet (142 meters), of which 200 feet (61 meters) would be the Ship. However, in his recent post, Musk stressed that the vehicle is probably closer to 150 meters in total height, suggesting the next Starship could be nearly 500 feet tall. The exact specifications for the V4 are still evolving, but the planned progression from V2 to V3 to V4 was previously detailed in a chart shared by Musk.

The successful recovery of the Ship was described by SpaceX’s Dan Huot as "the missing link" during the company’s webcast. Huot noted that catching the Starship changes everything for the company. The maneuver was particularly challenging because the Ship returns from orbit, entering the atmosphere faster and hotter than the booster. SpaceX had not attempted this specific tower catch for the upper stage prior to Flight 15, making the successful execution a major technical achievement for the program.
summary: Elon Musk stated that the next-generation Starship V4 will be approximately 70 meters long, representing a 40% length increase over the current model. The V4 variant will feature nine Raptor-Vacuum engines and allow for more than 60% more propellant load.
author: Space.com

title: Arecibo Observatory Sends First Interstellar Message to M13 in 1974
content:
On November 16, 1974, scientists transmitted humanity’s first intentional interstellar message using the Arecibo Observatory radio telescope in Puerto Rico. At the time, the facility housed the largest radio telescope in the world. The signal was directed toward the M13 star cluster, located 25,000 light-years away, meaning it will take 25,000 years for the message to arrive if extraterrestrial life exists there.

The message was designed by Cornell University astronomy professor Frank Drake, graduate students Richard Isaacman and Linda May, and Arecibo staff member James Walker, with input from astronomer Carl Sagan. The transmission consisted of 1,679 bits arranged in 73 lines of 23 characters, utilizing prime numbers to aid decoding. The content included information about human DNA, figures of a human, the solar system, and the Arecibo telescope itself.

According to the SETI Institute, the broadcast was the most powerful ever beamed into space at that time. It utilized Arecibo’s megawatt transmitter attached to its 305-meter antenna, creating an emission equivalent to a 20 trillion watt omnidirectional broadcast. SETI noted that such a signal would be detectable by a SETI experiment anywhere in the galaxy, assuming a receiving antenna of similar size.

The broadcast lasted less than three minutes. As of 2026, the message has traveled approximately 52 light-years, with 24,948 light-years remaining before it reaches M13. While this was the first intentional olive branch to the stars, subsequent efforts have included messages on spacecraft like Pioneer and Voyager, as well as a 2008 broadcast of Paul McCartney’s “Across the Universe” by NASA.
summary: On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials.

title: Kate Nash Launches 'Butts for Tour Buses' Protest, Uses OnlyFans to Fund Tour
content: She threw a (metaphorical) brick through Spotify’s window and exposed industry failings with her ‘Butts for Tour Buses’ campaign. Now the singer is embracing her Irish roots with her new album’s fighting spirit Kate Nash was standing on a fire truck in a showgirl outfit complete with white tights and pink G-string, shouting through a loudhailer about the music industry’s failure to pay artists fairly, when she wondered if she’d gone too far. It was 2024 and the truck, which made pit stops outside the London offices of Spotify and Live Nation, had a large black-and-white picture of Nash’s bum on the back along with the words “Butts for Tour Buses” – a reference to her newly launched OnlyFans account, which she was using to fund her tour. That afternoon, she called her manager Kat. “I told her: ‘I’ve thrown a brick through the window at Spotify.’ She went: ‘What, literally?’ and I said: ‘No, but I’ve been standing outside their offices with a megaphone, so that relationship is over. I don’t think we’ll be making their New Music Friday feature.’ And we didn’t.” [see footnote]
summary: Kate Nash staged a protest outside Spotify and Live Nation offices by standing on a fire truck with a megaphone and a picture of her bum, promoting her 'Butts for Tour Buses' campaign. She used an OnlyFans account to fund her tour and announced she would no longer be featured on Spotify’s New Music Friday.

I hear it and I accept this conviction,” and added, “I address my deep and sincere apologies to those who suffered.” This marks the first time Depardieu publicly apologized to the victims of the 2021 incident.

title: Writer Finds Comfort in Wonder Boys, 2000 Film
content:
In a recent series featuring writers selecting their most comforting rewatches, one contributor shares their appreciation for Wonder Boys, a 2000 comedy drama directed by Curtis Hanson. Although the writer admits to being generally allergic to films and books centered on writers, including washed-up novelists and creative writing professors, they hold a special place for this particular movie. The author credits the film with influencing their decision to become a writer, having first seen it on its opening weekend at the age of 17. The image of poring over novels with kindred spirits in a sun-dappled seminar room at a liberal arts college, where the author enrolled a year later, held endless appeal.

The film stars Michael Douglas as Grady Tripp, a rumpled creative writing professor who struggles to finish his second novel while maintaining an affair with his boss’s wife. The narrative unfolds on the eve of the university’s annual literary festival, when Grady faces a series of personal crises. His wife leaves him, and his lover, Sara, announces she is pregnant with his child. Additionally, his brilliant but troubled student, James Leer, arrives at the festival’s kick-off party holding what may or may not be a cap gun. Leer is described as a student who can rattle off Hollywood suicides in alphabetical order.

Despite the chaotic circumstances, Grady responds to these events with the urgency of a veteran pot smoker, a character trait explicitly noted in the source. The writer found even these misadventures romantic during their initial viewing, highlighting the film’s impact on their perspective of academic life and creative pursuits.
summary: The writer, who has spent two decades writing about writers, cites Wonder Boys as a comforting rewatch. The 2000 film follows creative writing professor Grady Tripp, who struggles to finish his second novel and has an affair with his boss’s wife.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Raye Leads Female-Heavy Grammys 2027 Nominations with 11 Nods
content:

Raye leads the female‑heavy race with 11 nominations, marking her fourth nomination overall. She is nominated for Song of the Year, Songwriter of the Year and Album of the Year. Beyoncé has earned a record‑breaking 100th nomination across all major categories.

title: Russell Brand: Open Secret Doc Pays Tribute to Journalists Exposing Him
content: This Netflix documentary offers a fascinating look at how Brand’s behaviour wasn’t simply tolerated; it was actively celebrated Last week was quite the week. Coming within a few days of each other, the sentencing of Russell Brand and the allegations about David Walliams have felt dizzying. As well as all the elation that justice has been served in relation to Brand, and the admiration for the women who saw that it was, there’s also an underlying sense of exhaustion about the sheer grubbiness of it all. With this in mind, the thought of watching a feature-length documentary about the Sunday Times and Channel 4’s investigation into Brand might feel like willingly dunking your head into a toilet. However, Russell Brand: Open Secret is absolutely worth an hour and a half of your time. Not only is the film a tribute to Rosamund Urwin and Charlotte Wace, the journalists who spent years meticulously drawing the net closer to Brand – and, needless to say, to his victims – but it does a tremendous job of putting the whole sorry affair into a broader cultural context.
summary: The Netflix documentary Russell Brand: Open Secret examines how Brand's misconduct was celebrated and details the investigation by the Sunday Times and Channel 4. It pays tribute to journalists Rosamund Urwin and Charlotte Wace who spent years uncovering the case and to the victims.

title: John Oliver Criticizes Trump’s Everglades Immigration Prison as 'Utter Disgrace'
content: The Last Week Tonight host memorialized the performative cruelty of Trump’s short-lived immigration prison in the Florida Everglades John Oliver opened the season finale of Last Week Tonight with a brief reaction to the Federal Aviation Administration’s shock grounding of all US flights on Friday afternoon, which brought nationwide travel to a halt and stranded travelers across the country. He zoned in on transportation secretary Sean Duffy, whose Friday press conference in the midst of a crisis left much to be desired. “Rather than use that press conference to dispense information, which would have been ideal, he instead took it as an opportunity to air grievances and make demands,” Oliver noted. Duffy blamed “old, legacy equipment that failed” and asked for $50bn from Congress to upgrade the system. “I can’t build things if i don’t have money,” Duffy said. “I want $50bn. title: Nathan Fielder draws most attention at Governors' Awards as Glenn Close and John Malkovich react
content:
The Governors’ Awards drew a full house of Hollywood’s biggest stars, but the event remained sober and orderly. No one was reported to have become intoxicated, and the main attraction was an awkward moment involving documentarian‑turned‑actor Timothée Chalamet.

At just after 6 p.m., Academy president Lynette Howell Taylor was working to seat a crowd of roughly 700 people in the Ray Dolby Ballroom. She warned that she would call out anyone still standing by name if they did not take a seat immediately. Chalamet was the sole person still on his feet, circling the table where he was supposed to sit beside his girlfriend, Kylie Jenner, opposite Tom Holland and Zendaya. Taylor allowed him a brief grace period before he finally took his seat.

The ceremony’s setting felt oddly school‑like, with a faded, striped carpet and a social structure that was closed‑off and insular. Cliques, alliances, legendary enmities, and intricate hierarchies of popularity and influence were evident. Some attendees—Chalamet, Holland, Tom Cruise, Matt Damon, Willem Dafoe, and Seth Rogen—appeared comfortable, while others seemed to be still vying for a better table.
summary: Nathan Fielder draws most attention at Governors' Awards as Glenn Close and John Malkovich react.

title: Ineos settles with Ben Ainslie over America's Cup yacht dispute
content:
Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos Group has reached an out-of-court settlement with Sir Ben Ainslie regarding a dispute over the £180m yacht built for the 2024 America’s Cup. The agreement resolves Ineos’s claim that Ainslie refused to return the vessel, a matter for which the group had sought £10m in damages. This settlement concludes legal proceedings that had been scheduled for a trial in 2028.

The two parties previously collaborated closely during two America’s Cup cycles, culminating in Ineos Britannia becoming the first British crew to win the challenger series two years ago. However, their partnership dissolved over plans for a third bid, with Ineos announcing last year that it had “reluctantly withdrawn its challenge” for the 2027 event in Naples.
summary: Ineos Group has reached an out-of-court settlement with Sir Ben Ainslie regarding a £10m claim over the refusal to return a yacht. The agreement ends a plan for a 2028 trial over the vessel built for the 2024 America's Cup.

title: Switzerland defeat Scotland, raising doubts over Pocognoli's suitability
content:
A Scotland–Switzerland match that was expected to be a long‑running contest instead ended in a brief, four‑minute affair. Andy Robertson reached a milestone, becoming Scotland’s most capped player, but the game’s outcome left him wishing the moment had arrived under different circumstances.

Scotland’s defeat came at the hands of a second‑string Swiss side, prompting questions about the suitability of Sébastien Pocognoli to lead the national team. The Scottish FA’s enthusiasm for Pocognoli as Steve Clarke’s successor has been described as increasingly “ridiculous” in light of the result.

After the match, Robertson remarked, “I don’t think you’ve got time in international football,” underscoring the disappointment felt by the Scottish camp.

title: Pochettino says he would advise Guardiola to take US coaching job
content:
Mauricio Pochettino, the outgoing head coach of the United States national team, is preparing to leave for a role at Manchester United. In recent remarks he discussed what changes he would make to soccer in America, reflecting on his experience in the national program.

Pochettino and Pep Guardiola share a long, storied history. As players, Guardiola was at Barcelona while Pochettino was rising at Espanyol. As managers, they faced each other 22 times in the Premier League, and both have expressed mutual respect and a shared intensity in their coaching philosophies.

During Guardiola’s September visit to Yankee Stadium, where he served as a pre‑match hype man for New York City FC’s rivalry game against Red Bull New York, Pochettino was in town to scout the match. He sat with Guardiola throughout the game, accompanied by his assistant coach Jesús Pérez and US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson.
summary: Pochettino says he would advise Guardiola to take US coaching job.

title: COP31 draft climate deal urges faster shift from fossil fuels
content:
COP31 has released a draft of the cover decision that ties together the summit’s outcomes, and the text calls for a faster shift away from fossil fuels. The draft is now being examined by diplomats, journalists, activists and scientists.

During a press conference, Australia’s climate minister Chris Bowen, who is also president of the negotiations, said it “is a given” that parties will not reach agreement on every element of the draft. He noted that the timing of this COP, alongside the rise of artificial intelligence, war and cost‑of‑living crises, makes it important to demonstrate that multilateralism works, adding that the world wants action on climate change amid a “polycrisis.”

Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley described the “cancer of indifference” to the climate crisis as pushing the world closer to the brink. Further expert analysis of the draft will follow.
summary: A draft cover decision released at COP31 calls for a faster shift away from fossil fuels. Australia’s climate minister Chris Bowen said parties will not agree on all elements of the draft, and Mia Mottley warned that indifference to the climate crisis is pushing the world toward the brink.

title: Cop31 draft text aims to draw out parties, says Australia’s talks president
content: Many countries surprised to see first version delivered with more than four days of negotiation remaining A draft text of a possible final outcome from the Cop31 UN climate summit is an attempt to “draw out parties” on their areas of agreement and disagreement, Australia’s president of the talks has said. Many countries were surprised to see a first draft of a potential “cover decision” from the fortnight-long talks early on Monday afternoon, with more than four days of negotiation still to go. The text includes several proposals regarded as highly contentious by some countries, including a call to “immediately transition away from fossil fuels”.
summary: The president of the Cop31 talks, Australia’s president of the talks, said the draft text is meant to “draw out parties” on areas of agreement and disagreement. title: EPA’s Aspect chemical-detection plane grounded during Oklahoma leak, Texas fire, Ohio blasts
content:
The EPA’s Aspect chemical-detection plane, once a critical tool for monitoring toxic substances during disasters, has frequently remained grounded in recent years. The aircraft did not deploy during an ammonia leak in Weatherford, Oklahoma, that injured 74 people last November, nor during a March fire at a Valero refinery in Port Arthur, Texas, or August blasts at a recycling plant in Toledo, Ohio, which killed two workers.

Mark Thomas, a former EPA official who managed the program for 18 years, noted that the plane would have responded to all these incidents a decade ago. The article highlights this decline in operational readiness while also inviting readers to submit climate questions for upcoming Stateside guest Bill McKibben.
summary: EPA’s Aspect chemical-detection plane grounded during Oklahoma leak, Texas fire, Ohio blasts.

title: Cape Cod harvester Ernie Eldredge finds non‑native clam, signaling invasion
content:
Shellfish harvester Ernie Eldredge was working ankle‑deep in the tidal flats of Chatham, Massachusetts, on Cape Cod when he encountered an unfamiliar clam in a 2023 harvest. After pulling his rake through fine white sand without hearing the usual “clink” of shells, Eldredge set the specimen aside and consulted a scientist for identification. Together they determined that the mollusk was a potentially harmful, non‑native species, marking what Eldredge described as the start of an invasion.

Eldredge noted that the tidal flats on the elbow of Cape Cod are constantly shifting, with recent fall winds bringing additional sand into the area. He observed that the clams he had been finding over the summer may have moved on, prompting his continued search across the changing landscape.
summary: Shellfish harvester Ernie Eldredge discovered an unfamiliar mollusk in his 2023 haul on Cape Cod’s tidal flats in Chatham, Massachusetts. He consulted a scientist who identified it as a potentially harmful non‑native species, indicating the start of an invasion.
