title: Wadden Sea faces danger list threat from extraction, tourism, and fishing
content:
The Wadden Sea, a vast intertidal system spanning the coasts of the Netherlands, Germany, and Denmark, faces potential inclusion on the UNESCO World Heritage in Danger list. This unique habitat, recognized as the largest unbroken system of intertidal sand and mud flats globally, was granted World Heritage status in 2009. The area is characterized by a dramatic transformation in its landscape, shifting from unbroken water with offshore sandy islands at high tide to a complex maze of deep channels, drying sandbanks, salt marshes, and mud flats a few hours later.

Despite its ecological significance and rich marine life, the Wadden Sea is under pressure from various human activities. Extraction industries, tourism, and fishing are cited as factors taking a toll on the environment. These pressures threaten the integrity of the habitat that supports a wealth of biodiversity, prompting concerns about its current status and future conservation efforts within the World Heritage framework.
summary: The Wadden Sea, a transboundary intertidal system spanning the Netherlands, Germany, and Denmark, was awarded UNESCO World Heritage status in 2009. Extraction industries, tourism, and fishing are currently taking a toll on the region's marine life and bird populations.

title: UK EV target cuts would hurt car industry, ministers warned
content:
Experts have warned that weakening the United Kingdom’s zero‑emissions vehicle (ZEV) mandate would slow the electric‑vehicle market and hinder efforts to reduce the cost of living. They argue that such moves would hurt the car industry, consumers, campaigners and the broader economy.  

The Climate Change Committee (CCC) is scheduled to write to ministers on Wednesday, outlining how changes to the ZEV mandate could affect the cost of living and the country’s net‑zero targets.
summary: Campaigners and experts warn that weakening the UK's zero emissions vehicle mandate would slow the market and harm consumers. The climate change committee is set to write to ministers about the impact of these changes on the cost of living and net zero targets.

title: Huge waves up to 50ft force pier closures on California coast
content:
Large waves up to 50 feet flooded southern California streets and prompted evacuation warnings near coastal cities. The California coast was pummeled on Sunday by these huge waves, which inundated beaches, flooded local streets, and forced the closure of popular piers.

Additionally, the National Weather Service office for the San Francisco Bay Area warned that surf up to 35 feet (11 meters) was possible, along with dangerous rip currents and sneaker waves.
summary: Large waves up to 50ft flooded southern California streets and prompted an evacuation warning near a coastal city, forcing the closure of popular piers. title: Ice Baths: Popular Recovery Method for Athletes and Gym-Goers
content: Ice baths have become one of the most popular recovery strategies in sport. They are used by elite athletes and recreational gym‑goers to reduce soreness and recuperate more quickly after exercising.
summary: Ice baths have become a popular recovery strategy in sport. They are used by elite athletes and recreational gym-goers to reduce soreness and recover more quickly after exercising.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Standardized Markers Let Labs Reliably Isolate Thymic Epithelial Cells
content: Standardized markers and extraction methods now allow laboratories to reliably isolate thymic epithelial cells (TECs). These “teacher” cells, which instruct immune T cells to attack foreign invaders while preventing attacks on healthy tissues, comprise less than 1 % of all cells in the thymus gland. Because TECs are so rare, research groups have spent decades struggling to agree on how to properly study them. The new protocols provide a consistent approach, enabling more accurate and reproducible investigations of this critical component of the immune system.
summary: The thymus gland uses rare “teacher” cells, thymic epithelial cells (TECs), to train immune T cells to attack foreign invaders and prevent autoimmunity. Researchers have spent decades struggling to isolate TECs, which make up less than 1% of all cells in the gland.
author: Medical Xpress

title: National poll: Parents say pets boost kids' emotional health but expect them to care
content: A national poll found that most parents say pets benefit children’s emotional health, yet they still expect kids to help with care. Parents note that when a new pet arrives as a holiday or birthday surprise, children often do not follow through on the pet‑care responsibilities they anticipate.
summary: Most parents say pets benefit children's emotional health. Parents expect kids to help with care, but kids may not always follow through on the pet‑care responsibilities.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Inpatient Alcohol Treatment Group Attendance Drops, Racial Gaps Persist
content:
A recent study published in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs found a steep decline in the use of mutual‑help groups among people in inpatient alcohol treatment.  The proportion of patients who attended Alcoholics Anonymous or a similar group at least once a week fell from more than half of the sample to fewer than four in ten over a seven‑year period.

The research also highlighted significant racial and ethnic disparities.  Latinx/Hispanic, Black, and American Indian/Alaska Native patients were less likely than white patients to attend weekly, even after the analysis adjusted for factors such as age, employment status, and alcohol use.
summary: Inpatient Alcohol Treatment Group Attendance Drops, Racial Gaps Persist.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Cannabis use disorder linked to higher odds of suicidal thoughts
content: Cannabis use is increasingly common and socially accepted, yet health risks exist, particularly with problematic use. A new study published by Rutgers University in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs found that adults with cannabis use disorder have significantly higher odds of suicidal ideation.
summary: A new study in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs found that adults with cannabis use disorder have significantly higher odds of suicidal ideation. The research was published by Rutgers University.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Archaeologists explore wealth inequality among Europe's early herders
content: Archaeologists are investigating the level of inequality in prehistoric societies, focusing on Europe’s early herders. They aim to determine how wealth and status can be measured in cultures that left no written records, tax registers, or census data.
summary: Archaeologists examine how unequal prehistoric European herding societies were. They consider ways to measure wealth in cultures lacking written records, tax registers or census data.
author: Phys.org

title: Lake Baikal, the world’s largest freshwater lake, shows signs of recovery
content:
Lake Baikal in Siberia, which contains roughly 20 % of the world’s surface freshwater, is described as the most voluminous freshwater lake and is now reported to be recovering after decades of decline. The lake was designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1996 because of its significant biodiversity.  

Over the past century Baikal experienced considerable decline, a trend linked to aridification spreading across East Asia, even as Lake Superior remains the largest freshwater lake by surface area. The recent recovery marks a reversal of that long‑term downturn.
summary: Lake Baikal in Siberia holds about 20% of the world’s surface freshwater, making it the most voluminous freshwater lake. After a century of decline linked to aridification across East Asia, the lake is now recovering.
author: Phys.org

title: Ancient 3.95‑billion‑year‑old rocks found in northern China illuminate early crust formation
content:
Earth is estimated to be about 4.5 billion years old, but rocks from its earliest era are exceedingly scarce. Researchers have identified a set of rocks in northern China that date to roughly 3.95 billion years ago, placing them among the oldest known specimens on the planet.

The newly discovered rocks are attracting attention because they provide fresh evidence about the processes that formed and altered Earth’s crust during its formative period.
summary: Rocks dating about 3.95 billion years were discovered in northern China, making them among the oldest known on Earth. They are revealing new clues about how Earth's crust formed and evolved.
author: Phys.org

title: Lens may let astronomers see supernova SN Ares two more times in ~70 years
content:
Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope identified an exploding star, designated SN Ares, whose light was magnified and split by the gravitational lensing of a massive galaxy cluster. The detection corresponds to a universe age of 4.9 billion years.  

A paper describing the find was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 23, and it includes a prediction for when the remaining distorted images of SN Ares are expected to arrive, suggesting the cosmic lens could reveal the same supernova two additional times over roughly a 70‑year span.
summary: Thanks to the gravitational lensing caused by a massive galaxy cluster and high-resolution images from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers discovered an exploding star when the universe was 4.9 billion years old. The discovery paper, posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct.
author: Phys.org

title: Eye‑tracking study probes cultural influence on art perception in Sudan’s Old Dongola
content: An eye‑tracking study conducted in Sudan investigated whether culture shapes how people view art. Separately, Old Dongola, situated on the banks of the Nile in northern Sudan, is now an abandoned settlement that looked very different hundreds of years ago.
summary: An eye‑tracking study was carried out in Sudan to examine whether culture shapes how people look at art. The research was set at Old Dongola, an abandoned settlement on the banks of the Nile in northern Sudan that looked very different hundreds of years ago.
author: Phys.org

title: White dwarf flashes radio waves every 8 minutes, paired with sun‑like red dwarf
content:
Since 2022, astronomers have been puzzled by a new class of objects known as long‑period radio transients. These sources emit bright flashes of radio waves into space at intervals ranging from a few minutes to a few hours.  

Some of these transients have been traced back to binary systems that consist of a small, dim, cool red dwarf and a white dwarf, a stellar remnant.
summary: A white dwarf is flashing bright radio waves about every eight minutes. It is in a binary system with a red dwarf that looks a lot like the Sun.
author: Phys.org

title: Aging stars can experience sudden drops in brightness
content: The article notes that, from a naked‑eye perspective, stars appear stable and predictable, with the Sun described as a low‑mass star expected to shine steadily for billions of years. It contrasts this with massive stars, which are rarer and contain many times the Sun’s mass. No mention is made of aging stars or sudden luminosity dips.
summary: Stars generally appear stable and predictable from a naked‑eye view. The Sun, a low‑mass star, is expected to shine steadily for billions of years, unlike rarer massive stars.
author: Phys.org

title: Four-month rehab after ACL surgery may protect young adults from early knee osteoarthritis
content:
A new study indicates that a specific exercise regimen may protect young adults from early knee osteoarthritis after anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) surgery. Researchers observed that participants who completed a four‑month supervised rehabilitation program experienced improvements in pain, muscle strength and quality of life, while the program did not damage knee cartilage.

The results counter concerns that exercise could exacerbate injured knees and suggest the protocol could influence future recovery approaches for patients undergoing ACL reconstruction.
summary: Researchers found that a four-month supervised rehabilitation program improved pain, muscle strength and quality of life after ACL surgery without damaging knee cartilage. The study suggests the exercise may protect young adults from early knee osteoarthritis and challenges fears that exercise worsens injured knees.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists develop simple method to convert coffee grounds into biodiesel
content: Scientists have developed an efficient method that converts used coffee grounds into a potential source of biodiesel while preserving the remaining material for other renewable fuels and valuable chemicals. The discovery suggests that millions of tons of discarded coffee waste could become a useful resource for sustainable energy.
summary: Scientists have created an efficient process that turns used coffee grounds into a potential source of biodiesel. The method also preserves leftover material for other renewable fuels and valuable chemicals, potentially converting millions of tons of coffee waste into sustainable energy.
author: Science Daily

title: Leonid meteor shower peaks this week, bright display expected 17‑18 November
content: The Leonid meteor shower, an annual display that appears to radiate from the constellation Leo in the eastern sky as Earth moves through a comet’s debris stream, is set to reach its peak this week. Observers are advised that the shower’s most active period will occur during the night of 17–18 November. Under ideal viewing conditions, up to 10–15 meteors per hour may be seen, offering a brief but bright spectacle despite modest overall numbers.
summary: The annual Leonid meteor shower reaches its peak this week, with the most active period on the night of 17–18 November. Under ideal conditions observers may see 10–15 meteors per hour, noted for their brilliance.
author: Guardian Science

title: Puncak Jaya Glaciers Shrink to Tiny Fragments, Near Disappearance
content:
The Indonesian Sudirman Range on the island of New Guinea contains one of the world’s few tropical glaciers.  NASA Earth Observatory’s latest images show the dramatic retreat of the ice that once capped the highest peaks of the range, including the summit of Puncak Jaya.  A false‑color image taken in 1988 by the Landsat 5 Thematic Mapper (TM) and a newer image from 2026 acquired by the Landsat 9 Operational Land Imager (OLI) are placed side by side.  In the older picture, blue‑shaded ice covers several ridges, while brown shows exposed rock and green indicates lower‑elevation vegetation.  The 2026 image reveals only small blue fragments of ice; the majority of the former glacial area is now bare brown rock.

In 1988 the glaciers on Puncak Jaya spanned roughly 4.31 square kilometers (1.66 square miles).  By September 2025 satellite and aerial data indicated that the ice had shrunk to about 0.09 square kilometers (0.03 square miles) – a loss of roughly 98 percent of the original extent.  The remaining ice is limited to a dozen soccer‑field‑sized patches.  An aerial survey scheduled for December 2026 is expected to provide a more precise estimate of the ice that remains in that year.

Thickness measurements at the primary monitoring site on the East Northwall Firn show a dramatic decline.  The ice was 32 meters (105 feet) thick in 2010, fell to 4 meters (13 feet) in 2023, and by November 2024 the ice at that location had disappeared entirely.  As the glaciers thin, they fragment, creating more exposed edges that accelerate melt.  The 2026 image shows freshly uncovered bedrock between the remaining ice remnants, and although snow still falls, it does not accumulate enough to rebuild the ice.

A glacier must be thick enough to flow downhill under its own weight and must receive more snowfall than melt.  The remaining ice at Puncak Jaya has thinned so far that it no longer flows; it exists only as stagnant patches.  “While small ice remnants persist in high‑altitude crevices around Puncak Jaya, their functional life as active glaciers is effectively over,” said Donaldi Permana, a climate scientist with the Indonesian Agency for Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics (BMKG).

Future projections suggest that the main glacial ice could disappear completely by around 2030, although BMKG estimates indicate an even earlier loss, potentially hastened by the current El Niño.  Past El Niño events have accelerated thinning: during 2015‑2016 the ice lost about 5.3 meters (17 feet) in a single year, and the 2023‑2024 El Niño saw a loss of 2 to 4 meters (7 to 13 feet) per year.  Ongoing satellite monitoring and the upcoming 2026 aerial survey will continue to track the final remnants of this tropical glacier.
summary: Puncak Jaya Glaciers Shrink to Tiny Fragments, Near Disappearance.
author: NASA News

title: APOD November 16, 2026: Webb Infrared Image Shows Star Formation and Jets in NGC 7129
content: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 16 – NGC… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. NGC 7129: Star Formation with Jets from Webb Explanation: How do stars form? To help answer this question, NASA used the James Webb Space Telescope to take the featured detailed image of the star-forming region NGC 7129 in infrared light. Star formation progresses when gravity pulls together massive amounts of gas, but soon things can get complicated when previously formed stars emit powerful jets and winds — and some then explode. Opaque dust can form in the cool atmospheres of stars and, when dispersed, can obstruct visible-light images. Many stars can be seen to be forming in the featured image, with the young stars on the left, in the gold-colored gas, typically being more mature than the young stars on the right — in the red region. Jets and wind s likely cause the filamentary nature of the red-colored gas. Studying stars at different stages of development bolsters understanding about what physical processes are most important and when. Tomorrow’s picture: sky duel Date: November 16, 2026 Credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, JWST ; Processing: A. Pagan ( STScI ) Authors & editors: Robert Nemiroff, Jerry Bonnell, Cecilia Chirenti, Keighley Rockcliffe A service of: ASD at NASA / GSFC, NASA Science Activation & Michigan Tech. U. summary: NASA used the James Webb Space Telescope to capture an infrared image of the star‑forming region NGC 7129 for the November 16, 2026 Astronomy Picture of the Day. The image shows many young stars, with jets and winds likely shaping the red‑colored gas and illustrating different stages of stellar development.
author: NASA News

title: Apple launches study to assess effectiveness of AI health tools
content:
Apple announced a new study aimed at better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful the tools’ responses are. The Apple Health AI Usage Study is being conducted in partnership with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform that generates answers from medical sources such as The New England Journal of Medicine.  

Participants will download a new iOS app, pose medical questions to the AI, and then rate each response on accuracy, detail and relevance. The app is now available for download, and enrollment in the study begins today.
summary: Apple launches study to assess effectiveness of AI health tools.
author: The Verge

title: Helsing backer Plural raises €1 billion ($1.1 billion) to fund Europe’s next moonshots
content: Operator‑led venture capital firm Plural, a backer of Helsing, has secured €1 billion in new capital (approximately $1.1 billion). The fund’s size places it alongside other sizable European investors such as Mundi Ventures’ Kembara and the EQT‑managed Scaleup Europe Fund.
summary: Helsing backer Plural, an operator-led VC firm, has raised €1 billion in new capital, equivalent to $1.1 billion. The fund joins other large European investors such as Mundi Ventures’ Kembara and the EQT-managed Scaleup Europe Fund.
author: TechCrunch

title: Centrelink client and childcare worker data may be fed into Palantir software used by ACIC
content:
An exclusive report reveals that personal information belonging to Centrelink customers, taxpayers and childcare workers is among the sensitive data being shared with the Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission (ACIC). The ACIC employs software from US technology firm Palantir, and the data may be flowing into Palantir’s surveillance platform without the originating departments being aware of the transfer.  

Guardian Australia reported in September that Palantir’s software is used by the ACIC within the multi‑agency fraud fusion taskforce, which was created in 2022 to target fraud in government payments from the National Disability Insurance Scheme, childcare and welfare programs.
summary: Personal information of Centrelink customers, taxpayers and childcare workers may be ending up in Palantir’s surveillance software in Australia. Palantir’s software is used by the Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission as part of a multi‑agency fraud fusion taskforce established in 2022 to target fraud in government payments.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Liberal Senator Andrew McLachlan says AI policy must protect artists' copyright
content:
Liberal senator Andrew McLachlan warned that artists’ copyright should not be “sacrificed” for corporate profit as Australia debates artificial‑intelligence policy. The South Australian backbencher said he prefers “real forests over virtual ones” and urged the Labor government to weigh AI’s impact on creators and the environment.

McLachlan criticised both his party’s and the Labor government’s approach, arguing that building new data centres should not be prioritised above environmental concerns. He noted that Labor is reviewing copyright changes as part of an AI policy suite that also covers data centres, online safety, energy resources and economic benefits.

The senator added that proposals to water down copyright law could raise constitutional challenges, suggesting such changes might constitute an illegal acquisition of property. The commentary was published alongside a call to subscribe to Guardian Australia’s politics newsletter.
summary: Liberal Senator Andrew McLachlan urged the Labor government to consider AI's impact on artists and the environment, saying art must not be sacrificed for corporate profit. He warned that weakening copyright law for AI could be an illegal acquisition of property and criticized prioritising new datacentres over real forests.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Lords report says UK faces polycrisis of cyber, sabotage and climate threats
content:
A parliamentary report from the House of Lords warns that ministers are “complacent” as the United Kingdom faces a “polycrisis” of fast‑changing, interconnected threats. The report calls for an urgent new approach to resilience planning to address cyber‑attacks, sabotage, and the climate crisis, and urges rapid action to boost national resilience to potentially major crises.

The report notes that most of the public are unaware of the scale of threats such as cyber‑attacks, proxy acts of violence, strikes on under‑sea cables, extreme weather and flooding. It also mentions that Labour has recently launched a “Be Ready” campaign encouraging households to keep supplies of food and water.
summary: Lords report says UK faces polycrisis of cyber, sabotage and climate threats.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Trump, Xi and Putin to meet in China, White House says
content: Trump is scheduled to leave Washington on Monday for the Philippines, where he will attend a meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations. After the ASEAN gathering, he will travel to Shenzhen in China.
summary: Trump will depart Washington on Monday for the Philippines. He will attend an ASEAN meeting there before heading to Shenzhen, China.
author: Euronews

title: Zelenskyy says US proposes Ukraine cede land to Russia for NATO membership
content: Russian President Vladimir Putin has said Russia will not abandon its territorial demands to control parts of Ukraine and has dismissed the proposal to deploy foreign peacekeeping troops in the country. No further details were provided.
summary: Zelenskyy claimed the United States is floating a proposal for Ukraine to give up territory to Russia in exchange for NATO membership. Putin said Russia will not back down on its territorial demands and rejected the idea of foreign peacekeeping troops being deployed in Ukraine.
author: Euronews

title: Euronews launches new season with live journalism, weeknight shows and new studio
content:
Euronews began its new season on 16 November, unveiling a fresh slate of live journalism, new weeknight programmes and a brand‑new studio. The network emphasises its journalists and editorial expertise as the focal point of coverage.  

The channel promises more perspectives and deeinsight into the stories shaping Europe, offering viewers a broader European focus in 12 languages.
summary: Euronews launches its new season today, 16 November, with more live journalism, new weeknight programmes and a brand‑new studio. The channel will offer more perspectives on stories shaping Europe and will broadcast in 12 languages.
author: Euronews

title: Pope Leo XIV calls for justice for slain Amazon defenders during Peru rainforest visit
content: Pope Leo XIV visited the Peruvian rainforest and demanded justice for slain Amazon defenders. He said, “The blood of these brothers cries out to God and demands justice,” to applause from a crowd many of whom wore feathered headdresses and face markings of the region.
summary: Pope Leo XIV said “The blood of these brothers cries out to God and demands justice” during his visit to the Peruvian rainforest. His words were met with applause from a crowd, many of whom wore feathered headdresses and face markings of the region.
author: Euronews

title: Ciryl Gane retains MMA heavyweight title against Josh Hokit at UFC 334
content:
Ciryl Gane retained his status as the world’s MMA heavyweight champion after defeating Josh Hokit in the main event of UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden in New York.  

The five‑round bout was described as rough by Shirli Sitbon.
summary: Ciryl Gane beat Josh Hokit in the main event of UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden in New York. The 5‑round fight was rough, according to Shirli Sitbon.
author: France 24

title: The week in pictures: Spain protests, Pope Leo's Peru 'homecoming' and Rocky fans in Philly
content:
France 24 reviewed a selection of striking images from the week, highlighting protests in Spain over a housing crisis that has dominated the election campaign.  

The recap also featured Pope Leo XIV’s visit to his adopted homeland Peru and fans of the film Rocky commemorating the 50th anniversary of its release.
summary: The week in pictures: Spain protests, Pope Leo's Peru 'homecoming' and Rocky fans in Philly.
author: France 24

title: US Investigates Nationwide Flight Ground Stop Amid Travel Disruptions
content:
A nationwide ground stop began Friday night, halting U.S. flights and leaving hundreds of thousands of passengers stranded. Travel disruptions were felt worldwide, but officials say air travel is expected to resume normal operations this Sunday.

The Trump administration attributed the stoppage to a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines and denied any cyberattack. The incident has prompted questions about the country’s aging infrastructure, and lawmakers are urging an investigation. Analysis is provided by Philip Mann, aviation expert at Vector Strategic Consulting.
summary: US air travel is expected to return to normal this Sunday, following a nationwide ground stop Friday night that stranded hundreds of thousands of passengers and disrupted travel worldwide. The Trump administration blamed the incident on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines and said there was no evidence this was a cyberattack.
author: France 24

title: Hundreds of thousands protest in Prague against plan to fund public media directly
content: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs gathered in Prague on Sunday to protest a government proposal to replace public‑media fees with direct state funding, a move critics argue could jeopardise broadcasters’ independence. Organisers claimed the turnout surpassed a March rally of more than 200,000, possibly making it the largest demonstration in the country since the 1989 Velvet Revolution.
summary: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday against the government's plan to replace public media fees with direct state funding. Organisers said the turnout exceeded a March protest of more than 200,000, possibly making it the largest demonstration since the 1989 Velvet Revolution.
author: France 24

title: Gadi Eisenkot says caretaker Netanyahu must quit over alleged aide election interference
content:
Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot announced on Sunday that caretaker premier Benjamin Netanyahu must leave office immediately after reports surfaced of alleged electoral interference by a Netanyahu aide.  

Eisenkot, a former army chief, described Netanyahu and his entourage as an immediate threat to democracy, making his remarks hours after representatives were discussing the formation of a national unity government.
summary: Prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot said caretaker premier Benjamin Netanyahu must leave office immediately after reports of alleged electoral interference by a Netanyahu aide. He called Netanyahu and his entourage an immediate threat to democracy, hours after representatives discussed forming a national unity government.
author: France 24

title: 600 Ukrainian drones intercepted over Moscow as Crimea bridge strike halts traffic
content:
Russian air defences intercepted 600 Ukrainian drones heading toward the Moscow region overnight and into Monday morning, according to Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin. The same period saw Ukraine strike the bridge that links Russia and Crimea across the Kerch Strait, a development reported by the peninsula’s Russia‑backed governor.

Russia’s Defence Ministry said its air‑defence systems downed a total of 1,336 drones over Russian regions during the overnight operation. The liveblog continues to track further developments.
summary: Russian air defenses intercepted 600 Ukrainian drones heading toward the Moscow region, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin said. Ukraine also struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea across the Kerch Strait, and the Defence Ministry reported 1,336 drones were downed over Russian regions overnight.
author: France 24

title: Oleshky evacuees receive first proper meals in years at Kyiv hospital
content: Patients recently evacuated from the Russian‑occupied town of Oleshky in Ukraine’s Kherson region are being served chicken soup, bread and buckwheat porridge in a Kyiv hospital corridor. Staff and volunteers push carts with the steaming meals, which evacuees say are the first proper meals they have had in years.
summary: Staff and volunteers in a Kyiv hospital corridor pushed carts with chicken soup, bread and buckwheat porridge to patients. The patients had recently been evacuated from Russian‑occupied Oleshky in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region.
author: UN News

title: Honduran farmer Anastacio Martínez Gómez faces drought in Central America's Dry Corridor
content: Across Central America’s Dry Corridor, farming families depend on rainfall. In southwestern Honduras, 73‑year‑old farmer Anastacio Martínez Gómez has spent most of his life learning to work the land, yet his experience alone cannot fully address the challenges when rains fail.
summary: Farming families across Central America’s Dry Corridor depend on seasonal rains. In southwestern Honduras, 73‑year‑old farmer Anastacio Martínez Gómez has spent his life learning to work the land, but his experience can only take him so far.
author: UN News

title: Nobel laureate Nadia Murad recounts ISIL atrocities against Yazidis
content: Nobel Peace Prize laureate Nadia Murad has spent years telling the world about the atrocities committed against her and the Yazidi community by militants from the terrorist group, ISIL.
summary: Nobel Peace Prize laureate Nadia Murad says she has taken her story back day by day. She has spent years telling the world about atrocities committed against her and the Yazidi community by ISIL militants.
author: UN News

title: Senior Hells Angel charged with threatening to kill reporter Nick McKenzie
content:
Victoria police have charged a man suspected of being a chapter president of the Hells Angels with threatening to kill Nine’s investigative reporter Nick McKenzie. The allegation comes from the Victorian police taskforce that is investigating corruption in the building sector.

According to police, detectives from the taskforce charged the man on Monday after he sent a number of allegedly threatening, offensive and abusive text messages to the reporter on Friday. The taskforce confirmed the charge and stated that the messages were directed at McKenzie, who works for the Age.
summary: Victoria police say a senior Hells Angel, suspected of being a chapter president, was charged with threatening to kill investigative reporter Nick McKenzie. Detectives from the Victorian taskforce investigating building‑sector corruption charged the man on Monday after he sent allegedly threatening, offensive and abusive text messages to the Age journalist on Friday.
author: Guardian World

title: Queensland, NT keep puberty blocker bans for transgender kids despite NHMRC advice
content:
Queensland health minister Tim Nicholls said the state’s position on banning puberty‑blocker treatment in public hospitals remains unchanged, even after new guidelines were issued.

Federal health minister Mark Butler expressed confidence that Queensland and the Northern Territory will consider the advice of the National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC). The federal government commissioned the NHMRC last year to develop guidance in response to the bans imposed by the two governments.
summary: Queensland, NT keep puberty blocker bans for transgender kids despite NHMRC advice.
author: Guardian World

title: University of Melbourne exam platform fails, hundreds of students abandon finals
content:
A technical failure on the University of Melbourne’s digital exam platform forced hundreds of students to abandon their final exams on Monday morning. The university said that “third‑party technical partners” were likely responsible for the outage.  

Many students were unable to access the platform at the start of the exam, leaving them in a state of limbo and unable to complete the assessment.  

Jol Scobie, a first‑year student, had been preparing for weeks for his Australian politics exam. He had originally been told earlier in the year that the test would be a handwritten essay, but instructors later changed it to a digital format.
summary: Hundreds of University of Melbourne students were forced to abandon their final exams on Monday morning after they could not access the digital platform required to start them. The university said third‑party technical partners were likely responsible for the platform failure.
author: Guardian World

title: Coles investigates cyber-attack, says no data compromised and urges password updates
content:
Australia’s second‑largest retailer, Coles, announced on Monday that it is investigating a cyber‑attack targeting its systems. The company said the investigation is being conducted with assistance from the Australian Cyber Security Centre and global security experts. Coles stated that, to date, no customer, team or supplier data has been compromised, but it remains too early to determine whether any information has been stolen.

The retailer apologized to customers and advised them to update their passwords as a precaution while the probe continues.
summary: Australia’s second‑largest retailer Coles said it was targeted in a cyber‑attack and is investigating the threat with the Australian Cyber Security Centre and global security experts. The company said no customer, team or supplier data had been compromised and advised people to update their passwords as a precaution.
author: Guardian World

title: MP Helen Haines discharged after alleged attack that caused double leg amputation
content:
Independent MP Helen Haines was discharged from hospital after four weeks in care following an alleged attack outside her electorate office in Victoria. The incident, which left her with the amputation of both legs, prompted her return to medical facilities.

In a statement released after her discharge, Haines said she was “overwhelmed” by the thousands of warm wishes she received. She thanked Australians for the charity donations that have helped her and announced that her recovery has moved into a rehabilitation stage, which will continue in Melbourne.
summary: Independent MP Helen Haines was discharged from hospital four weeks after she was allegedly attacked outside her Victorian electorate office, resulting in the amputation of both legs. She said she is overwhelmed by thousands of warm wishes, thanked Australians for charity donations and has moved to the rehabilitation stage of her recovery in Melbourne.
author: Guardian World

title: Megaspeed, the company linked to the downfall of Nvidia boss, says it’s a ‘legitimate and lawful business’
content:
Megaspeed International, a Singapore‑based cloud computing company linked to the downfall of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, says it is a legitimate and lawful business.  

The company announced that its director, who allegedly had an affair with Jensen Huang, left the business in late 2025, and that Alice Huang, accused of being a Chinese spy, also departed the company in that same period.  

Megaspeed said it is aware of recent media reports containing assertions about its business, supply chain and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence.
summary: Megaspeed, the company linked to the downfall of Nvidia boss, says it’s a ‘legitimate and lawful business’.
author: Guardian World

title: Canada may turn to Chinese automakers if US trade talks fail, Carney says
content:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said that if trade talks with U.S. President Donald Trump do not preserve an integrated North American auto industry, Canada could turn to Chinese automakers. Speaking in Cambodia on Monday, Carney added that “Canada is going to move forward either way” when asked whether Chinese investment was being used as leverage in the U.S. negotiations.

His remarks came ahead of a scheduled meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, where auto manufacturing is expected to be discussed. In January, the two leaders agreed to allow tens of thousands of Chinese electric vehicles into Canada at reduced tariffs.
summary: Canada may turn to Chinese automakers if US trade talks fail, Carney says.
author: Guardian World

title: Pope Leo XIV demands justice for Amazon defenders during Peru visit
content: Pontiff delivers forceful speech in Peru as he travels from high in the Andes into the Amazon Pope Leo XIV has demanded justice for environmental defenders killed for protecting the Amazon and backed efforts by Indigenous peoples to stop their lands from being ravaged by logging and illegal mining. On the penultimate day of his South American tour, Leo on Sunday travelled into the Peruvian Amazon and channelled one of Pope Francis’s core teachings that links care for the most vulnerable with care for God’s creation.
summary: Pope Leo XIV delivered a forceful speech in Peru, traveling from the Andes into the Peruvian Amazon on Sunday, the penultimate day of his South American tour. He demanded justice for environmental defenders killed protecting the Amazon and backed Indigenous efforts to stop logging and illegal mining.
author: Guardian World

title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
content:
On the night of November 15-16, stargazers in the United States can observe a close approach between Jupiter and Mars in the constellation Leo. The two planets will rise over the eastern horizon around midnight, appearing slightly more than 1 degree apart. This alignment occurs as the blue-white light of the star Regulus glows below them. According to In-The-Sky, the pair will not be this close again until July 2029.

Although the planets appear side by side, they are actually separated by over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers). The light from Regulus has traveled approximately 79 light-years to reach Earth. This visual phenomenon, known as an appulse, happens once every 2 to 2.5 years when Mars catches up to Jupiter in its more distant orbit.

Both Mars and Jupiter are superior planets, meaning their orbits are beyond Earth’s. Consequently, they always appear as full disks through a telescope, unlike Mercury and Venus which show phases. A 6-inch telescope can reveal distinct features of each world. Jupiter displays cloud bands and zones formed by ammonia and water masses moving through its hydrogen and helium atmosphere via jet streams. Mars appears as a reddish, ochre disk with dark surface features where basaltic rock is exposed after iron-rich dust has been scoured away, according to NASA.
summary: Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov.
author: Space.com

title: Apollo 12 Launches Nov. 14, 1969, Achieves Pinpoint Landing Near Surveyor 3
content:
On November 14, 1969, NASA launched the Apollo 12 mission, marking the second crewed landing on the moon. The crew consisted of commander Pete Conrad, lunar module pilot Alan Bean, and command module pilot Richard Gordon. While Gordon remained in the command module to orbit the moon, Conrad and Bean descended to the lunar surface. Unlike the previous Apollo 11 mission, which drifted from its planned landing zone, Apollo 12 achieved a pinpoint landing in the Ocean of Storms.

The primary scientific objective was to land near Surveyor 3, a robotic lander that had touched down on the moon more than two years prior. Scientists aimed to examine the spacecraft to assess its durability in the lunar environment. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited the lander and collected samples to return to Earth. Additionally, the crew gathered 75 pounds of moon rocks, most of which were basalts formed from molten lava. These samples indicated that the landing site was more than 3 billion years old.

The mission demonstrated that the Apollo program could consistently land in specific areas identified by geologists, proving that the Apollo 11 landing was not a one-off event. This capability was essential for future, more ambitious exploration. The launch also highlighted the importance of a well-prepared Mission Control team, which possessed detailed knowledge of the spacecraft’s systems. This expertise was critical for the program's success and would later prove vital during the Apollo 13 mission.
summary: Apollo 12 launched on Nov. 14, 1969, with commander Pete Conrad, pilot Alan Bean, and command module pilot Richard Gordon. The crew performed a pinpoint landing in the Ocean of Storms near Surveyor 3, collecting 75 pounds of basaltic moon rocks older than 3 billion years.
author: Space.com

title: Rory McIlroy Dedicates Record-Equalling Eighth Race to Dubai Title to Father
content:
Rory McIlroy has claimed a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title, a victory he emotionally dedicated to his father, Gerry, who is currently recovering from major surgery in the United States. McIlroy was moved to tears while recalling a parting message from his father, who had urged him to “Go and win the Race to Dubai” before McIlroy traveled to the closing events of the DP World Tour season.

The Northern Irishman finished second in the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai, posting a final round of 67. This result was sufficient to secure the season-long order of merit crown, allowing him to edge out Eugenio Chacarra by a narrow margin of 125 points. While Tyrrell Hatton won the tournament itself, Chacarra’s third-place finish meant McIlroy prevails in the overall standings. McIlroy later revealed that his father had been at the forefront of his mind throughout the competition.
summary: Rory McIlroy won his eighth Race to Dubai title after finishing second at the DP World Tour Championship, edging Eugenio Chacarra by 125 points. He dedicated the victory to his father, Gerry, who is recovering from major surgery in the United States.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Terry Butcher reflects on Maradona's Hand of God goal
content:
Former England centre-back Terry Butcher recently answered questions from Guardian readers in a London office during the week he was presented with his England legacy cap. The session addressed topics including his interactions with Diego Maradona and manager Bobby Robson. Butcher recalled the 1986 World Cup quarter-final against Argentina, where he was notably affected by Maradona’s “Hand of God” goal.

Butcher detailed a specific post-match encounter at the Azteca stadium, where he and Maradona were together in the doping-control room. He described tapping his head and then his hand to reference the controversial goal. Maradona responded by tapping his head, but did not acknowledge the handball. Butcher noted that Maradona avoided admitting to the infraction because doing so would have validated Butcher’s accusation.
summary: Terry Butcher, former England centre‑back, talks about the 1986 World Cup match against Argentina and Maradona’s Hand of God goal. He recalls being in the post‑match doping‑control room and noting that Maradona did not admit to the goal.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Wales Seismic Victory Over All Blacks in Cardiff
content: Seismic victory in Cardiff was cathartic and though Steve Tandy urges caution, maybe the ‘Welsh problem’ can be fixed So that’s that fixed then. Wales are back and all is right with the world. Suddenly the dysfunction at the union, the financial plight, the disputes, the emptying stadiums, the defeats – oh, the defeats – feel a very long way away. The All Blacks have been beaten. Seventy-three years of hurt, no more need for dreaming. The euphoria in the Principality Stadium, however many people were there – or more pertinently not – seemed as eerily familiar as it was cathartic. This was how Cardiff used to feel on match day.
summary: Wales won a seismic victory over the All Blacks in Cardiff, with Steve Tandy urging caution. The win ended 73 years of hurt and brought euphoria to the Principality Stadium, signalling Wales are back.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England's Three Lions win over Spain in two acts: first superb, second heroic
content:
Sid Lowe describes England’s victory over Spain as a match played in two distinct acts, with the first being superb and the second heroic. In the final, tense moments, the world champions continued to press, while England’s hold on possession had significantly declined. During this period, Dan Burn was substituted on, and the scoreboard displayed a 4-0 lead, but the clock seemed to move slowly as Spain kept returning to the attack.

Harry Kane left the bench to stand beside manager Thomas Tuchel, using hand gestures to direct his teammates to hold onto their lead. Tuchel nudged Kane playfully before fourth official Marc Bollengier ordered the captain back to the bench. However, Kane soon rejoined his teammates, who were standing together awaiting the conclusion of the game.

From the sideline, Kane witnessed James Trafford make a double save, a heroic moment that allowed England to survive the pressure. He also saw Dan Burn clear a final header just before the referee blew the whistle. Following the final whistle, Kane and his teammates ran back onto the pitch to celebrate the win.
summary: England beat Spain in a final where Dan Burn scored the decisive goal. Harry Kane and Thomas Tuchel guided the team, and James Trafford made a double save to secure the victory.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England boost squad with Furbank, Chessum and Atkinson for All Blacks clash
content:
England welcomed back the cavalry for the Saturday clash with the All Blacks, with full‑back George Furbank, Ollie Chessum and Seb Atkinson returning to the squad after injury.  

Steve Borthwick’s team are braced for a backlash following New Zealand’s first defeat by Wales in 73 years, but the head coach is boosted with the three key men on course to make their comebacks this weekend.
summary: England have recalled full-back George Furbank, lock Ollie Chessum and centre Seb Atkinson from injury for their upcoming match against New Zealand. Coach Steve Borthwick said the team is preparing for possible backlash after New Zealand suffered their first defeat by Wales in 73 years.

title: NFL roundup: Vikings win on Cousins’ return; Hutchinson reportedly ends season celebrating sack
content:
The Minnesota Vikings secured a 7‑2 victory over the Green Bay Packers, with Kirk Cousins leading the comeback after rejoining the team from the Las Vegas Raiders at the trade deadline. Cousins completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and threw two touchdown passes in his first game back, five days after the move. Levi Drake Rodriguez contributed two of the Vikings’ eight sacks in the win.

Other NFL highlights included Detroit’s fifth consecutive victory in Munich, Patrick Mahomes throwing five touchdown passes in a Chiefs win, and the Buffalo Bills improving to an 8‑1 record following their win over the Jets.

Cousins’ return came after his last appearance at Lambeau Field, when he tore his Achilles tendon in a 24‑10 Minnesota victory on October 29, 2023. His performance has revitalized a Vikings offense that had stalled under former quarterbacks Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz.
summary: NFL roundup: Vikings win on Cousins’ return; Hutchinson reportedly ends season celebrating sack.

title: Mirra Andreeva wins WTA Finals at Indian Wells, defeats Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3
content:
Mirra Andreeva captured the WTA Finals at Indian Wells by defeating Elina Svitolina 7‑5, 6‑3. The 19‑year‑old Russian earned the world No. 2 ranking and completed the tournament without losing a set.  

During the first set, Andreeva served for the break at 5‑4 but began the game with two double faults and two unforced errors, allowing Svitolina to take the break.  She quickly recovered, won the next five games, and regained momentum to close out the set.  

After regaining the break, Andreeva continued her strong play, securing a second‑set win and her first WTA Finals title.
summary: Mirra Andreeva defeated Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 to win the WTA Finals at Indian Wells for the first time. The victory earned her the world No 2 ranking and she dominated the tournament without losing a set.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England beat Spain after Anderson red to top Nations League group
content:
England secured first place in their Nations League group after a 3‑2 victory over Spain, a result that came on the back of a red card to England’s defender Anderson. The win was enough to top the group and move England ahead of Spain in the standings.

Spain entered the match with a remarkable record, having lost only once in 43 games—a penalty defeat to Portugal in last year’s Nations League final. Thomas Tuchel praised the team’s resilience, noting that Spain had “forgotten how to lose.” The match saw England hold off a spirited Spanish fightback, with the red card proving pivotal in maintaining the lead.

The scoreline echoed a historic encounter from 2018, when England beat Spain 3‑2 in Seville. That result is remembered as one of Sir Gareth Southgate’s most celebrated victories, and Tuchel felt the same excitement and confidence at the end of the recent game.
summary: England beat Spain after Anderson red to top Nations League group.

title: Predator-like scent triggers anxiety-related brain circuit in mice
content: A study reports that exposure to a predator‑like scent triggers activation of an anxiety‑related brain circuit in mice. Anxiety disorders affect about 4.4 % of the global population, and despite decades of neuroscientific research, their neural bases remain incompletely understood.
summary: A predator-like scent was found to activate an anxiety-related brain circuit in mice. Anxiety disorders affect about 4.4% of people worldwide, according to the World Health Organization, and their neural underpinnings are not yet fully understood.

title: Single CRISPR infusion keeps monkey triglycerides low for three years
content: A new experiment using CRISPR gene‑editing delivered a single infusion to monkeys and maintained low triglyceride levels for three years. The study notes that elevated LDL cholesterol and triglycerides are major contributors to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and that gene‑editing technologies could serve as an alternative to traditional lipid‑lowering medications. Researchers say the results demonstrate the potential to control blood fats through a lasting DNA change, which might eventually replace the need for daily drug doses.
summary: A single infusion of a gene‑editing treatment lowered triglyceride levels in monkeys for three years. The findings suggest a lasting DNA change could control blood fats and may replace daily medication.

content: Research presented at Neuroscience 2026, the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting, reports strong connections between physical health and brain health in the context of Alzheimer’s disease and aging, expanding current understanding of how bodily factors relate to the neurodegenerative condition.

content: Recent advancements in brain‑computer interfaces are enabling clinical trial participants who cannot speak or make voluntary movements to restore communication. The new findings on these technologies were presented at Neuroscience 2026, the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting.
summary: Recent advancements in brain‑computer interfaces are helping restore communication in clinical trial participants who have lost the ability to speak or make voluntary movements. The new findings were presented at Neuroscience 2026, the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience.

content: New evidence supports the idea that differences within and between sexes impact how neurological disorders progress and respond to treatment. The findings were presented at Neuroscience 2026, the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience.
summary: New evidence shows that sex-based differences influence the progression and treatment response of neurological disorders such as pain, inflammation and Alzheimer's disease. The findings were presented at Neuroscience 2026, the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience.

title: Urban growth in São Paulo Metro Area collapses stream food webs, cutting connections
content:
Urban expansion in Brazil’s São Paulo Metropolitan Area is driving the collapse of food webs in local streams, according to a new study. The research links the advance of urbanization directly to severe ecological disruption in these waterways.

Published in August in the journal Nature Cities, the study finds that degradation does more than reduce species numbers; it selectively removes organisms according to size and streamlines ecological interactions. As a result, the complexity of stream networks falls dramatically, with connections dropping from 190 to just three.
summary: Urbanization in the São Paulo Metropolitan Area is causing the collapse of food webs in local streams. A study published in August in the journal Nature Cities found that degradation selectively eliminates organisms by size, simplifying ecological interactions and reducing network connections from 190 to three.

title: New study independently checks accuracy of 2019 Event Horizon Telescope black hole image
content: A new study has produced an independent assessment of the iconic black‑hole image released by the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration on April 10 2019. The photograph shows the supermassive black hole at the center of galaxy M87, located roughly 55 million light‑years from Earth.
summary: A new study provides an independent assessment of the iconic black‑hole image’s accuracy. The Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration released the first picture of the black hole at the center of galaxy M87, about 55 million light‑years away, on April 10 2019.

title: ALMA finds three dense cores at different stages in region G40.282−0.219
content: Astronomers using ALMA have identified three dense cores at distinct evolutionary stages within the massive star‑forming region G40.282−0.219. The finding highlights physical and chemical differences among the cores that coexist inside the same massive dense gas clump.
summary: Astronomers have revealed three dense cores at different evolutionary stages within the massive star-forming region G40.282−0.219, shedding light on the physical and chemical differences among cores within the same massive dense clump.

title: 125,000‑year‑old Uruq al‑Julaybah lakeside site sheds light on early human life in Saudi Arabia
content: Archaeologists recovered megafauna remains, stone tools and rare plant material from the 125,000‑year‑old lakeside site of Uruq al‑Julaybah in Mundafan, southern Saudi Arabia. The assemblage offers a detailed view of prehistoric human life, showing how early people lived, hunted and utilized their environment during a greener, wetter phase in Arabian history.
summary: Megafauna remains, stone tools and rare plant material were recovered from the 125,000‑year‑old lakeside site of Uruq al‑Julaybah in Mundafan, southern Saudi Arabia. The discoveries provide a detailed picture of how early people lived, hunted and used their environment during a greener, wetter period in Arabian history.

title: Archaeologists uncover Danish skeleton that witnessed agriculture's rise
content: Archaeologists have examined an immaculately preserved Mesolithic skeleton from Denmark using radiocarbon dating and isotope analysis. The results show the individual lived through the onset of agriculture and altered his diet accordingly, offering a rare “eyewitness” perspective on the Neolithic revolution.
summary: Radiocarbon dating and isotope analysis of an immaculately preserved Mesolithic skeleton from Denmark show the individual lived through the introduction of agriculture. The study indicates the person adapted his diet to the change, providing a unique eyewitness account of the Neolithic revolution.

title: Study finds school attended predicts parents' education hopes in high segregation areas
content: A study finds that in highly segregated areas, the specific school a child attends is closely linked to the number of years of education parents expect their child to complete. The research highlights the school environment’s influence on shaping parental educational hopes.
summary: Where segregation is high, the school a child attends is closely linked to the number of years of education parents expect their child to complete. The study suggests the school environment plays a key role in shaping parents' educational hopes for their children.
author: Phys.org

title: Milk and wine found in 2,000‑year‑old Menorcan funerary vessels
content:
Archaeologists have identified milk and wine as remnants of funerary rituals in Menorca dating to the Late Iron Age, or post-Talayotic period, over 2,000 years ago. During this era, the Balearic Islands experienced increased connectivity with the wider Mediterranean while maintaining local traditions, such as burying the dead in rock-cut tombs or artificial caves. These sites often featured external courtyards in front of burial chambers where animal offerings were likely made.

Researchers had previously suspected that perishable foods or liquids were offered in characteristic high-bottomed ceramic vessels, but the specific contents of these containers had never been identified until now. This discovery provides new insight into the distinct funerary practices of the region during a time of growing external contact.
summary: In the Late Iron Age, over 2,000 years ago, Menorca’s rock‑cut tombs contained ceramic containers. Analysis shows those containers held milk and wine, indicating perishable food and liquid offerings in island funerary rituals.
author: Phys.org

title: Danish 6000‑year‑old “Rødhals Man” skeleton linked to arrival of farming
content: Clues about the diet of “Rødhals Man”, who lived some 6000 years ago, hint that he lived through one of the most revolutionary changes in human history
summary: A skeleton discovered in Denmark has been identified as “Rødhals Man”, who lived roughly 6000 years ago. Dietary clues suggest he lived through the transition to farming, a major shift in human history.

title: Stanford scientists find hidden brain signals that predict Alzheimer’s years early
content: Stanford researchers have identified hidden patterns of brain activity that can predict Alzheimer’s risk years before memory problems emerge, offering a potential early warning beyond traditional biomarkers. The same activity patterns also indicate brains that are unusually resistant to aging, suggesting possible avenues for future treatments aimed at protecting memory.
summary: Stanford researchers discovered hidden patterns of brain activity that can predict Alzheimer’s risk years before memory problems appear. The same patterns also reveal which brains are unusually resistant to aging, raising hopes for future treatments to protect memory.

title: Astronomers discover potential new dwarf planet 2026 ED138 beyond Pluto
content: Astronomers have identified a new object, designated 2026 ED138, that may be an enormous dwarf planet located beyond Pluto. The body, hidden for years in a densely populated area of the night sky, could increase the number of recognized dwarf planets and suggests additional distant worlds may exist beyond Neptune.
summary: Astronomers have uncovered a potentially enormous new dwarf planet beyond Pluto, called 2026 ED138. Its discovery could expand the solar system’s official dwarf‑planet family and hints that more mysterious worlds may be lurking far beyond Neptune.

title: Scientists develop new fiber supplement that improves gut health in IBS
content: Scientists have developed a new fiber supplement designed for people with irritable bowel syndrome. The blend improves gut health without increasing bloating, pain or other digestive symptoms, also lessens gut‑related anxiety while rapidly altering gut bacteria, suggesting a possible new approach to managing IBS and could help millions with the condition.
summary: Scientists have developed a new fiber supplement that improves gut health in people with irritable bowel syndrome without worsening bloating, pain, or other digestive symptoms. The supplement also reduced gut‑related anxiety and produced rapid changes in gut bacteria.

title: AI finds hidden heart signal that may predict sudden cardiac death
content: Scientists report that an artificial‑intelligence system identified a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that can predict sudden cardiac death before it occurs. The AI‑based method outperformed conventional screening approaches and may uncover thousands of individuals at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that could otherwise be missed by doctors.
summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods and could identify thousands of people at risk that doctors might otherwise miss.

title: Drone survey finds stable and declining Erect‑crested penguin populations in NZ
content:
A drone survey of New Zealand’s endangered erect‑crested penguins has identified a stark contrast in population trends. One group has remained stable for decades, while another has fallen by more than 40 percent, a decline attributed to predators, worsening storms and changing ocean conditions.

The study also found that the tiny Bounty Islands host nearly as many breeding pairs as the much larger Antipodes Islands, even though the Bounty Islands are about 40 times smaller in area.
summary: A drone survey of New Zealand’s endangered Erect‑crested penguins shows one population has remained stable for decades while another has declined by more than 40%, linked to predators, worsening storms and changing ocean conditions. The tiny Bounty Islands support nearly as many breeding pairs as the Antipodes Islands despite being about 40 times smaller.
author: Science Daily

title: Physicists use laser flashes to align tiny electrical regions in crystal
content: Physicists have shown that brief flashes of laser light can arrange tiny electrical regions within a crystal, a technique that resolves a longstanding mystery about the material’s behavior. The laser‑induced alignment persists for only a trillionth of a second, but researchers say the finding may enable new methods for processing and storing information.
summary: Scientists discovered that flashes of laser light can organize tiny electrical regions inside a crystal, solving a decades‑old mystery about the material’s behavior. The laser‑induced alignment lasts just a trillionth of a second, but the breakthrough could open the door to new ways of processing and storing information.

title: Fossil teeth show dinosaurs ate seaweed over 100 million years ago
content: New research has identified chemical signatures in fossilized dinosaur teeth that point to the consumption of seaweed and other marine foods more than 100 million years ago. The analysis suggests coastal dinosaurs and other prehistoric animals incorporated nutrients originating from the sea into their diets. The study further indicates that marine resources moved through ancient food chains, providing supplemental nutrition to a range of species, from herbivorous dinosaurs to carnivorous predators.
summary: Researchers found chemical signatures in fossilized dinosaur teeth that indicate they consumed seaweed and other marine foods more than 100 million years ago. The evidence suggests coastal dinosaurs and other prehistoric animals incorporated marine nutrients into their diets, supplementing both herbivores and predators.
author: Science Daily

title: ESA's Euclid telescope finds 31 ancient quasars, two as bright as a trillion suns
content: ESA’s Euclid space telescope has identified 31 ancient quasars, including two that emitted light comparable to a trillion Suns when the Universe was roughly 670 million years old. Powered by supermassive black holes, these quasars illuminate a period when the first galaxies were still coalescing.
summary: ESA’s Euclid space telescope discovered 31 ancient quasars. Two of the quasars shone with the brightness of a trillion Suns when the Universe was just 670 million years old, powered by supermassive black holes and showing a time when the first galaxies were still taking shape.
author: Science Daily

title: Stripe closes small business account after $1,500 invoice, citing unauthorized payment risk
content:
A small business that connects homeowners with local contractors posted on Hacker News that its Stripe account was closed after a single $1,500 invoice was blocked. The company’s model bills contractors per appointment that actually occurs. After a recorded call in which a client agreed to the arrangement, the client saved his card through a $1 Stripe payment link, which was successfully processed. Weeks later the business invoiced the client for three completed appointments, charging the saved card for $1,500. Stripe blocked the payment and, two days later, terminated the account, stating that the payments “don’t appear to have been authorized by the customer.”

The business appealed through the Stripe Dashboard, submitting an appeal letter, company documents and the invoice. The appeal was rejected the next day as an “unacceptable level of risk.” Support replied that the business model “presents a level of risk we’re unable to support” and that the decision was final. After an internal escalation, Stripe sent a brief email reaffirming that it would not accept payments for the business. The company notes that Stripe never requested the call recording, the client’s messages, or direct confirmation from the client, who says he has not disputed the charge and will pay by bank transfer outside Stripe.

The poster asks whether anyone at Stripe can review the evidence, including a call with the client, and seeks advice from others who have faced similar issues on how to structure per‑appointment billing to avoid the appearance of unauthorized charges. The original Hacker News thread has attracted 108 points and 36 comments.
summary: We're a small business that sells pre-booked appointments with homeowners to local contractors, billed per appointment that actually happens. Our first client agreed to this on a recorded call and saved his card through a $1 Stripe payment link, which we planned to use for billing later.
author: Hacker News

title: Free app enables SteamOS virtual machine on Apple Silicon Macs
content: A free application allows users to boot SteamOS within a virtual machine on Apple Silicon Macs. By running SteamOS this way, the Mac can access PC and legacy games that would not otherwise run on the hardware.
summary: A free application allows users to boot SteamOS in a virtual machine on an Apple Silicon Mac. This setup unlocks PC and legacy games that would not otherwise run on the Mac.
author: Wired

title: Rumors suggest Jensen Huang may seek return as Nvidia CEO, backed by Musk, Sweeney
content:
Nvidia co‑founder and former CEO Jensen Huang is at the center of a rapidly evolving drama.  The latest edition of the Stepback newsletter has been released to bring readers up to speed, and new developments have already emerged since that morning.  

Rumors now suggest that Huang may be seeking a path back to the CEO position.  In addition, Megaspeed has issued a statement claiming that Alice Huang has not worked for the company since August 2025, a claim that has raised further questions.  

High‑profile figures such as Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have publicly expressed support for a public letter demanding that Nvidia “bring Jensen back.”
summary: The drama around Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang is evolving quickly. The latest edition of our Stepback newsletter should get you up to speed, but there have already been a number of new developments since this morning.

title: ULA Vulcan rocket fails 10 minutes after launch, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites
content:
United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket lifted off on 15 November 2026 carrying 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites. The launch, conducted from Space Launch Complex 41, ended in failure when the vehicle experienced an anomaly about ten minutes after liftoff, according to a statement posted by ULA on X.

The mishap marks the first mission failure in ULA’s 20‑year operational history and prevented the delivery of the 40 Leo satellites to orbit. The launch was intended to be the first of 38 flights that Amazon has contracted with ULA. Leo, Amazon’s broadband satellite system and a competitor to SpaceX’s Starlink, has so far placed only a small portion of the satellites needed to challenge Starlink.
summary: ULA's Vulcan rocket lifted off on November 15, 2026 from Space Launch Complex 41 carrying 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites. An anomaly occurred about 10 minutes into flight, marking ULA's first mission failure in its 20‑year history and destroying the satellites.
author: The Verge

title: Armand Hammer releases surprise album Snakes & Ladders
content:
A surprise Armand Hammer record titled Snakes & Ladders was released this week. The album is a collaboration between Billy Woods and Elucid.

The reviewer notes that, while the production lacks the seamless through‑line of the duo’s previous Alchemist collaborations (Haram and Mercy), the album presents a singular vision. It features ominous background noises, blasts of industrial‑style rage, throbbing bass lines and saxophone bleats, and the reviewer affirms that Woods and Elucid continue to demonstrate excellent taste in production.
summary: Armand Hammer's album Snakes & Ladders dropped this week as a surprise release. The record, featuring Billy Woods and Elucid, is praised as one of their best despite lacking the seamless production of their Alchemist collaborations such as Haram and Mercy.
author: The Verge

title: ULA Vulcan rocket crashes minutes after liftoff, aborting Amazon satellite launch
content:
United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket, carrying 40 Amazon low‑Earth‑orbit broadband satellites, fell back to Earth minutes after liftoff on Sunday. The failure halted the mission that was intended to launch the first of 38 Vulcan flights Amazon has booked to expand its satellite internet network, which aims to compete with SpaceX’s Starlink.

The incident affects a vehicle that holds contracts to launch roughly half of the United States military’s national‑security space missions in the coming years. ULA officials indicated the rocket will remain grounded for an indefinite period while the cause is investigated.

Vulcan has previously experienced close calls, having encountered failures with its strap‑on solid rocket boosters on two of its four earlier flights. In those cases the rocket corrected the problems, completed orbit insertion, and subsequent months‑long reviews allowed the program to resume. Sunday’s mishap now adds another pause to the launch schedule.
summary: ULA Vulcan rocket crashes minutes after liftoff, aborting Amazon satellite launch.

content: Calls for governments to recognise sexual exploitation of children as preventable public health emergency Reports of artificial intelligence being used to sexually exploit children have risen by more than 8,400% in two years, research has found. A report by the Edinburgh-based Childlight – Global Child Safety Institute says AI-related child abuse material, including deepfakes using “nudify apps”, had risen from about 4,700 in 2023 to more than 400,000 in 2025.

content: Pope Leo XIV, 71, is continuing his South American tour despite large crowds gathering to see him. Health officials in Latin America say the crowds raise concerns, noting a surge in measles cases across the region this year.

content: Canada and the Philippines have concluded talks on a free‑trade agreement, Mark Carney announced to reporters. He said the outcome is “good news for Canadians” in agriculture, aerospace, artificial intelligence and for businesses involved in forest products, mining, energy, services and related sectors.
summary: Canada and the Philippines concluded talks on a free trade agreement, according to Mark Carney. Carney said the outcome is good news for Canadian agriculture, aerospace, AI and businesses in forest products, mining, energy and services.

content: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang invested heavily in open‑source AI, backing French‑founded Hugging Face and supplying chips to Mistral’s data centres, while opposing Washington’s restriction attempts. content: Ivory Coast, currently heavily reliant on fossil fuels, is pursuing solar power to enhance the sustainability of its energy consumption. The country recently inaugurated a new solar power plant in Ferkessédougou, located in the north, in July. This facility is projected to generate nearly 90 gigawatt-hours of electricity annually.
summary: Ivory Coast remains heavily dependent on fossil fuels and is exploring solar power to make its energy consumption greener and more sustainable. A new solar power plant in Ferkessédougou in the north, inaugurated in July, is expected to generate nearly 90 gigawatt‑hours of electricity a year, according to a report by Julia Guggenheim.

content: In South London, a “Santa school” is already in full swing as the holiday season approaches. The training venue, organized by the event company Ministry of Fun, gathers Santa impersonators, elves, and Mrs Clauses for a festive workshop. Participants share experiences, rehearse belly laughs, and learn techniques to convey the magic of Christmas. The initiative aims to prepare performers for upcoming holiday celebrations, according to a story by Rachael Griffiths.
summary: Many Santa impersonators are heading to a festive training school in South London. The school, organised by an event company called Ministry of Fun, brings together Santas, elves and Mrs Clauses to share experiences, practice belly laughs and learn how to bring Christmas magic to life.

content: President Trump is set to travel to Asia in a few days to meet President Putin and President Xi. The delegation may include one fewer tech executive, as Jensen Huang has recently resigned from Nvidia amid a suspected spy affair.

content: Spain’s coastguard said that nearly 2,200 migrants reached the Canary Islands in the past two days, extending a recent surge of arrivals from West African countries. The Spanish authorities declared a migration emergency in the archipelago earlier this week.
summary: Nearly 2,200 migrants have reached the Canary Islands over the past two days, Spain’s coastguard said Sunday. The arrivals continue a recent surge from West African countries, where authorities declared a migration emergency earlier this week.

content: Eli Junior Kroupi netted his first goal for France as Les Bleus defeated Turkey 2‑1 in Bordeaux on Sunday, moving to the top of their Nations League group with 13 points and securing a quarter‑final berth. Among the possible opponents in the last eight are World Cup winners Spain, who were beaten at home by England.

content: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, a founder of Mexico’s Guadalajara cartel known as the “boss of bosses”, died in hospital on Sunday aged 80 after suffering multiple organ failure, Jalisco state’s security ministry said. Imprisoned since 1989, he had been transferred from prison to the hospital two days before his death.
summary: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, a founder of Mexico’s Guadalajara cartel known as the “boss of bosses”, died in a hospital on Sunday at age 80 after multiple organ failure, Jalisco state’s security ministry said. He had been imprisoned since 1989 and was transferred from prison to the hospital two days before his death.

content: Elon Musk and an Uber co‑founder signed a petition that, by Sunday, counted more than 158,000 signatures calling for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia chief while an independent investigation proceeds. Huang resigned Thursday after disclosures of two extramarital affairs—one with a subordinate and another with a woman alleged to have spied for China—ending his 33‑year tenure.

Huang resigned Thursday after revelations of two extramarital affairs, one with a subordinate and another with a woman accused of spying for China, ending his 33‑year tenure.

content: Poland’s abortion laws are described as very restrictive. In response, activists have introduced the “Abortomat,” a locker that dispenses abortion pills to women seeking to end a pregnancy. The initiative encounters fierce opposition.
